The clause «نطمس …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «نردها …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نطمس.
The clause «نلعنهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نطمس.
The clause «لعنّا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «كان أمر الله مفعولا» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مفعولا): passive participle of the verb فعل يفعل, of the bāb of فتح; its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
1- «مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهاً»: in the indefiniteness of الوجوه, which conveys multitude, there is an intensification of the gravity of the matter, and in its vagueness there is gentleness toward those addressed and a fine summoning of them to faith.
2- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope): in His saying, the Exalted, «وجوها», where He mentioned faces and meant their owners, the relation being that of the whole.

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters); (الله) is the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative (manṣūb); (لا) is negating; (يغفر) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle; (يشرك) is an imperfect verb, passive, accusative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو», referring to the associating (al-ishrāk) or to the worshipped deity understood from the context of the verse; (الباء) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يشرك).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يشرك به) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by يغفر, i.e. «لا يغفر الإشراك به».
(الواو) is a conjunction; (يغفر) is like the first; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; (دون) is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (ذلك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) …, and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (اللام) is a preposition; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (يغفر); (يشاء) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (الواو) is resumptive — or a conjunction —; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يشرك) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يشرك); (الفاء) links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (افترى) is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (إثما) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, by افترى being made to carry the meaning of «اقترف»; (عظيما) is a naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يغفر …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يغفر …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «يشرك به» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يغفر …» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يغفر «[Note: al-ʿUkbarī rejected the conjunction so that an affirmative would not be conjoined to a negative; so in his view it is resumptive.]».
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «من يشرك بالله» (the nominal one) has no grammatical position, resumptive — or conjoined to the first resumptive clause.
The clause «يشرك بالله» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «افترى …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(افترى): the verb contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion (qalb); its original form is افتري — with a yāʾ at its end —; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted into an alif. (Āl ʿImrān — 94).

safi-cedvel:82-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for rebuking interrogation; (الفاء) conjunction; (لا) negative; (يتدبرون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (القرآن) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) resumptive; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun (ism) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of كان; (غير) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو; (وجدوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (وجدوا); (اختلافا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (كثيرا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «يتدبرون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.:
أيعرضون فلا يتدبرون ("Do they turn away, and so not reflect?").
The clause «كان ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «وجدوا ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.

* Benefits:
The harmony of the Quran:
- Absolute, comprehensive, complete harmony is the phenomenon that whoever reflects on the Quran can never miss. The phenomenon of the absence of discrepancy appears, first of all, in the Quranic expression, in terms of its delivery and its artistic methods ... For in human speech there appear peaks and foothills, success and stumbling, strength and weakness, soaring and descent, fluttering and heaviness, radiance and dimming, and the rest of the phenomena in which human traits become manifest, the most particular of them being the trait of "change" and constant variation from one state to another. This appears clearly in human speech, in the works of a single writer, a single thinker or a single artist.
It is clear that the opposite of this phenomenon is constancy and harmony, and this is what we notice in the Quran. There is a single level in this inimitable Book; its colours vary with the variety of the subjects it treats, but it is united in level and horizon, preserving perfection in its delivery, bearing the stamp of divine workmanship and pointing to the Majestic Maker.
And if the difference between the workmanship of Allah and the workmanship of man is perfectly clear on the side of verbal expression and artistic delivery, it is even clearer on the side of thought, organization and legislation. There is no human doctrine that does not bear the human stamp: partiality of view and vision, and temporary influence by problems. The opposite of that is what characterizes the comprehensive, integrated Quranic method, whose foundations are as constant as the laws of the universe.

safi-cedvel:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (إذا) an adverb for the future containing the sense of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis أذاعوا; (جاء) a past verb and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أمر) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (من الأمن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of أمر; (أو) conjunction; (الخوف) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الأمن, genitive like it; (أذاعوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أذاعوا) [Note: The verb was made to include the sense of تحدّث ("to speak of"), so it was made transitive with al-bāʾ.] , (الواو) conjunction; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (ردّوا) like أذاعوا, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (إلى الرسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ردّوه); (الواو) conjunction; (إلى أولي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ردّوه); the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, since it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (الأمر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أولي الأمر; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو; (علم) a past verb and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil; (يستنبطونه) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil ...
and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi; (منهم) like the first, attached to (علمه) [Note: The pronoun in (منهم) refers to the Messenger and to those in authority, or to others; there are many divergent opinions on its interpretation, and the meaning here, as stated in al-Baḥr of Abū Ḥayyān, is: «If they had refrained from plunging into what] [Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source.] , (الواو) resumptive; (لولا) a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd) — a non-jussive conditional — (فضل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and the khabar (predicate) is necessarily omitted, its implied form being "موجود" ("existing"); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (عليكم) like منهم, attached to a ḥāl of فضل الله [Note: Or attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) فضل.] , (الواو) conjunction; (رحمة) maʿṭūf to فضل, nominative like it, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لولا; (اتبعتم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; (الشيطان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (قليلا) excepted (mustathnā), accusative [Note: There are several views on the thing from which the exception is made (al-mustathnā minhu): the first, it is the agent of اتبعتم; the second, it is the agent of أذاعوا, i.e. they made known the security or the fear, except a few; the third, it is the agent of علمه, i.e. those who draw it out.
The fourth, it is the agent of وجدوا. The fifth: that those addressed in His saying (لاتبعتم) are all people in general, and what is meant by "the few" is the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. End of quotation, abridged from the Ḥāshiya of al-Jamal.] .
The clause «جاءهم أمر ...» is in the position of genitive through the annexation of (إذا) to it.
The clause «أذاعوا به ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ردّوه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the conditional clause with its verb, and its apodosis, which is conjoined to a resumptive clause preceding in the previous verse.
The clause «علمه الذين ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of the condition لو.
The clause «يستنبطونه ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «فضل الله (موجود) ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «اتّبعتم ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition (لولا).

* Morphology:
(أذاعوا): it contains iʿlāl (phonological change) by conversion; its origin is أذيعوا; the vowel was transferred to the dhāl before the yāʾ, and it was converted into an alif because the yāʾ was originally vowelled.

* Benefits:
الشيطان ("devil") is applied to:
Every insolent rebel among the jinn, humans and beasts. Jarīr said:
أيام يدعونني الشيطان من غزل، ... وهن يهوينني إذ كنت شيطانا
(The days when they would call me "the devil" for my love-poetry, while they loved me, since I was a devil.)
And when a thing is considered ugly it is likened to devils, so it is said: "as if his face were a devil". The devil is not seen, but it is felt that he is the ugliest of things, and if he were seen he would be seen in the ugliest form.
2- The merit of deliberation:
In this verse there is a censure of whoever rushes into matters before verifying them, and reports them and spreads them, when they may have no truth.
It is reported in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet ﷺ said: «It is enough lying for a man to relate everything he hears» .
Let us mention here the ḥadīth of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, agreed upon as authentic, when it reached him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had divorced his wives. He came from his house until he entered the mosque and found the people saying that, and he could not wait until he sought permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ and asked him: "Have you divorced your wives?" He said: «No». So I said: "Allahu akbar", and he mentioned the ḥadīth in full. [Translator's note: the source shifts here to the first person «فقلت» ("so I said"), as in ʿUmar's own narration.]

safi-cedvel:84-84.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (قاتل) an imperative verb; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta"; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of قاتل; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (لا) negative; (تكلّف) a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta"; (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (نفس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; in the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: عمل نفسك ("the deeds of yourself"); (الواو) conjunction; (حرّض) like قاتل, its last letter given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (عسى) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of عسى, nominative; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يكف) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (بأس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكف) is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of عسى.
(الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (أشد) khabar, nominative; (بأسا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (أشد) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first, nominative; (تنكيلا) tamyīz, accusative.
The clause «قاتل ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: إن أفردوك وتركوك فقاتل ("if they leave you alone and abandon you, then fight") [Note: Abū Ḥayyān preferred that the clause be conjoined to the clause of the preceding speech without connection to the condition, the address being to the Prophet ﷺ alone.] .
The clause «لا تكلف إلا نفسك» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of قاتل [Note: It may be resumptive with no grammatical position, or parenthetical between the two conjoined clauses.] .
The clause «حرّض المؤمنين» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause قاتل.
The clause «عسى الله ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason, or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يكفّ ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «الله أشد بأسا» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(تنكيلا): a regular maṣdar (verbal noun) of the four-letter verb نكّل; its pattern is تفعيل, with the addition of a tāʾ at the beginning of the past form, the lightening (un-doubling) of the ʿayn, and the addition of a yāʾ before the final letter.

* Benefits:
The saying of Allah the Exalted: لا تُكَلَّفُ إِلَّا نَفْسَكَ — إلا is a particle of restriction and نفسك is a second mafʿūl bihi, because the implied nāʾib fāʿil "anta" stands as the first object. إلا is parsed as a particle of restriction in two cases:
1- When the exception is complete (i.e. the thing excepted from is mentioned) and negated (i.e. preceded by a negation), and the noun after it is a badal (substitute) of the thing excepted from, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ما فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ مِنْهُمْ — bearing in mind that in this case it is permissible to put the noun after it in the accusative as an excepted.
2- When the exception is incomplete (i.e. the thing excepted from is not mentioned) and negated, as in this verse and in the saying of Allah the Exalted: وَما مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ.
So if the noun after إلا is not put in the accusative as an excepted, it is a particle of restriction.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (ليس) a defective, non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine; (التوبة) the noun of laysa, nominative (marfūʿ); (للذين) its i'rab was given in the preceding verse; attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of laysa [Note: it appears from the context of the verse that (التوبة) here is the maṣdar of "تاب المذنب إلى الله", i.e. the sinner turned back from his sin.. and for this reason it is valid for the preposition phrase (للذين) to be the khabar.], (يعملون السيّئات) like (يعملون السوء) in the preceding verse, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (حتّى) a particle of inception; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), attached to (قال), (حضر) a past verb; (أحد) a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الموت) fāʿil (agent), nominative, and it is with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the causes of death or its occasions; (قال) like (حضر), and the fāʿil is "he"; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the noun of inna; (تبت) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and (التاء) the fāʿil; (الآن) an adverb of time, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative, attached to (تبت), (الواو) conjunctive; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; (الذين) a relative in the position of the genitive (majrūr), maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first relative; (يموتون) like (يعملون) — in the preceding verse —; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (كفّار) khabar, nominative; (أولئك) its i'rab has passed — in the preceding verse —; (أعتدنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) the fāʿil; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أعتدنا), (عذابا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (أليما) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «ليست التوبة للذين..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (إنّما التوبة).
The clause «يعملون السيّئات» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «حضر أحدهم الموت» is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of (إذا) to it [Note: and the condition (إذا), its protasis and its apodosis form a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.].
The clause «قال..» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «إنّي تبت ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تبت الآن» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «يموتون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «هم كفّار» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «أولئك اعتدنا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أعتدنا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).

* Morphology:
(اعتدنا): it contains a substitution (ibdāl); its original form is أعددنا, and the first dāl was replaced with a tāʾ because they share one point of articulation, and they are often substituted for one another; its pattern is أفعلنا.

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative (manṣūb), and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, a badal (substitute) of (أيّ) — or a naʿt (adjective) of it —; (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (لا) negative; (يحلّ) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحلّ), (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (ترثوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (النساء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (كرها) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "compelling them to that".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ترثوا ...) is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of the verb (يحلّ).
(الواو) conjunctive; (لا) the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā; (تعضلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (اللام) the lām of cause (taʿlīl); (تذهبوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (ببعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تذهبوا), (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (آتيتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) an agent pronoun, and (الواو) a redundant letter for the lengthening (ishbāʿ) of the ḍamma of the mīm, and (هنّ) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تذهبوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (تعضلوهنّ).
(إلّا) a particle of exception; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يأتين) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, and (النون) the nūn of the feminine plural — the fāʿil; (بفاحشة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتين), (مبيّنة) a naʿt of (فاحشة), genitive like it.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتين ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, the implied form being "except in the committing of the indecency", and the preposition phrase is attached to an omitted ḥāl excepted from the generality of states [Note: and the meaning is: preventing women [from marrying] is not lawful in any state except the state of committing manifest indecency.].
(الواو) conjunctive; (عاشروا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (بالمعروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the agent of (عاشروهنّ) [Note: it may be attached to the verb (عاشروا).], (الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كرهتموهنّ) like (آتيتموهنّ), and the verb is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (عسى) a complete past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa; (أن تكرهوا) like (أن ترثوا); (شيئا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكرهوا..) is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of complete (عسى).
(الواو) the wāw of accompaniment (maʿiyya); (يجعل) an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the wāw of accompaniment; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يجعل) [Note: or to an omitted second object of (يجعل), which takes two objects.
(2, 3) It is permissible to conjoin the clause to the clause (لا يحلّ), i.e. to conjoin a performative (inshāʾ) to an informative (khabar), [since] [Translator's note: the source has «أنّ», evidently for «لأنّ», "because".] the negation here has the force of a prohibition, and the meaning is: do not inherit women by compulsion.. And conjoining a performative to an informative is permitted by Sībawayh in every case.], (خيرا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (كثيرا) naʿt, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجعل ...) is conjoined to a maṣdar cast from the preceding speech, i.e.: "there may be hope of dislike from you and of the placing of good by Allah".
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يحلّ» لكم [Translator's note: the source places «لكم» outside the quotation marks; reproduced as written.] has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «ترثوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «لا تعضلوهنّ» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (لا يحلّ) «2».
The clause «تذهبوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «آتيتموهنّ» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يأتين ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «عاشروهنّ» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (لا يحلّ) «3».
The clause «إن كرهتموهنّ» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «عسى أن تكرهوا ...» has no grammatical position, a causal explanation of the implied apodosis, i.e.: "if you dislike them, then be patient, because it may be that you dislike ...".
The clause «تكرهوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the fourth particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يجعل الله» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the fifth particle-relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(مبيّنة): the feminine of مبيّن, an active participle from the quadriliteral بيّن; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (أردتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) an agent pronoun; (استبدال) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (زوج) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (مكان) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (استبدال); (زوج) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (آتيتم) like (أردتم), and the verb has no position; (إحدى) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa; (هنّ) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (قنطارا) the second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لا) the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā; (تأخذوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تأخذوا), (شيئا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الهمزة) for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; (تأخذوا) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has (تأخذونه).] an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (بهتانا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent [Note: or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).. and likewise (إثما).], (الواو) conjunctive; (إثما) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (بهتانا), accusative like it; (مبينا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «إن أردتم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آتيتم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) supplied.
The clause «لا تأخذوا ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تأخذونه ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(استبدال): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the six-letter verb استبدل; its pattern is استفعال.. on the pattern of its past tense, with kasra on its third letter and the addition of an alif before its last letter.
(مكان): a noun of place from the triliteral كان; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the ʿayn, because the ʿayn of the verb in the imperfect has ḍamma ... In the word there is a weak-letter change (iʿlāl); its original form is مكون with sukūn on the kāf and fatḥa on the wāw; the wāw was converted to an alif after being made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the kāf..
(بهتان): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb بهت يبهت, of the bāb of فتح; its pattern is فعلان with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and the verb has another maṣdar, بهت, with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is for disapproval and rebuke; (تأخذون) its i'rab was given in the preceding verse; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (أفضى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (بعض) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلى بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أفضى), (الواو) conjunctive; (أخذن) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (النون) the fāʿil; (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to (أخذن), (ميثاقا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (غليظا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «تأخذونه..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أفضى بعضكم.» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «أخذن.» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.

* Morphology:
(أفضى): it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion (qalb); its original form is أفضي; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to an alif. Its pattern is أفعل, and the yāʾ was originally a wāw.

* Rhetoric:
- Metonymy (kināya): in His saying, Exalted is He: «وَقَدْ أَفْضى بَعْضُكُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ».
The expression is a metonymy for sexual intercourse, and the Arabs only use it for what one is shy to mention, such as intercourse.

* Benefits:
1- Among the subtleties of the Arabic language is the use of the word al-ifḍāʾ as a metonymy for intercourse; that is more conducive to social propriety and more elevated in taste, which shrinks from frankness regarding sexual matters. There is much of this in the course of the Noble Quran.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لا) the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā; (تنكحوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: (ما) is used here for rational beings, i.e. the wives of the fathers; it is a Quranic style that puts the rational in the place of the non-rational and vice versa for a rhetorical reason and a deep meaning (see verse 3 of this sūra).], (نكح) a past verb; (آباء) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من النساء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative by disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) [Note: because the prohibition is for the future, and what has passed is past.], (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (سلف) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it", referring back to (ما) [Note: (ما) may mean the marrying, or it may mean the wives.], and it is the referring pronoun; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna, the reference being to the sons' marrying the fathers' wives; (كان) a defective past verb, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it"; (فاحشة) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative; (الواو) conjunctive; (مقتا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (فاحشة), accusative like it; (الواو) conjunctive; (ساء) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it" [Note: the pronoun may be the pronoun of the defective verb, i.e. "its way was evil".. and it may be vague, specified by the tamyīz (سبيلا); (ساء) is then a non-inflecting (jāmid) verb for expressing blame..
and the one specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "the way of that marriage".], (سبيلا) tamyīz (specification), accusative, transferred from the fāʿil.
The clause «لا تنكحوا..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نكح آباؤكم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (ما).
The clause «قد سلف» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «إنّه كان فاحشة» has no grammatical position, a causal explanation of the prohibition.
The clause «كان فاحشة» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «ساء سبيلا» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted [word] conjoined to the khabar of kāna, its implied form being: "it being said of it: evil is it as a way" [Note: the clause (ساء سبيلا) may be resumptive with no grammatical position if the verb is made one of the verbs of blame.].

* Morphology:
(مقتا): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb مقت يمقت, of the bāb of نصر; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(ساء): it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion (qalb); its original form is سوأ, its imperfect يسوء; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to an alif.

* Rhetoric:
- In this verse there is the device of hyperbole (mubālagha) in His saying «إِلَّا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ».
It conveys hyperbole in the prohibition by casting the speech in the form of making it conditional on the impossible, the aim being to block the way of permission entirely; its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: «حَتَّى يَلِجَ الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِياطِ».

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الناس) a badal (substitute) from أيّ, following it in the nominative in form — or a naʿt (adjective) of it —; (اتّقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ربّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, naʿt of ربّ; (خلق) a past verb and (كم) a pronoun, direct object, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa", and it is the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid); (من نفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلقكم); (واحدة) naʿt of نفس, genitive (majrūr) like it; (الواو) a conjunction; (خلق) like the first; (من) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (خلق); (زوج) a direct object, accusative, and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (بثّ) like خلق; (منهما) like the first, attached to (بثّ); (رجالا) a direct object, accusative; (كثيرا) naʿt, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (نساء) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (رجالا), accusative like it; (الواو) a conjunction; (اتّقوا الله) like اتّقوا ربّ; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, naʿt of the Name of Majesty; (تساءلون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), with one of the two tāʾs deleted from it.. and the wāw is the agent; (به) like منها, attached to (تساءلون); (الواو) a conjunction; (الأرحام) conjoined to the Name of Majesty, accusative like it.. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (كان) an incomplete past verb, its noun a latent pronoun, implied as "huwa"; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (رقيبا), which is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الناس» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «اتّقوا ربّكم» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «خلقكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «بثّ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause خلق.
The clause «اتّقوا الله» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اتّقوا ربّكم.
The clause «تساءلون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
The clause «إنّ الله كان ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كان عليكم رقيبا» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(تساءلون) its original is تتساءلون; one of the two tāʾs was deleted for lightness.
(رقيبا) an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) from رقب يرقب, of the pattern (bāb) نصر; its wazn is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this noble verse is the device of an artful opening (barāʿat al-istihlāl): He opened the surah by pointing to the beginning of creation and formation, alluded to the important role of woman, and enjoined maintaining the ties of kinship.

* Benefits:
1- A pointer of the utmost importance: He, Glorified be He, opened His speech in this surah pointing to the most miraculous of matters in His creation, Glorified be He, namely life, whose basis is maleness and femaleness. This problem of «pairing» (al-zawjiyya) has occupied philosophers, ancient and modern, and many of them inferred the greatness and oneness of Allah from this angle, saying: it is impossible for the blind chance with which nature has been described to guide to the adoption of maleness and femaleness as a means of the continuation of the species in hundreds, nay thousands, of species, and on a single pattern. There must be a God, powerful and willing, who holds the helm of life, directs it in its true direction, sets its laws, and perfects its making and origination.
2- We alluded earlier in the book to the i'rab of «أي», and that it is used as a means to address a noun made definite with «ال». We point out here that it has other uses, the mention of which we see as completing the benefit, so we say:
3- «[Translator's note: so numbered in the source; this begins the list of uses, as «a-».]» The interrogative أي, by which the specification of a thing is sought, as in «أي رجل جاء» ؟ (which man came?) and أية امرأت جاءت؟ (which woman came?) «[Translator's note: so spelled in the source, «امرأت».]». b- It may include the meaning of a condition and so put two imperfect verbs in the jussive, as in «أي رجل يستقم ينجح» (whichever man is upright succeeds).
c- It may come to indicate the meaning of perfection, and is called «أيّ of perfection» (ayy al-kamāliyya), as in «خالد رجل أيّ رجل» (Khālid is a man, and what a man!). It is used only in annexation, and is parsed as an adjective after an indefinite and as a ḥāl (circumstantial) after a definite.
d- It comes as a link for addressing what contains «ال», as we have seen, and is followed by the hāʾ of alerting, as in «يا أيها الناس».
e- It may be a relative noun.
In all its states it is declinable with the three vowels, except for the relative أي when it is annexed and the first part of its ṣila is omitted, as in the saying of the Exalted «ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمنِ عِتِيًّا»; in this case it may be either indeclinable or declinable, and indeclinability is more eloquent.

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (آتوا) like اتّقوا in the previous verse; (اليتامى) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif; (أموال) a second direct object, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā, jussive-governing; (تتبدلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الخبيث) a direct object, accusative; (بالطيّب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تتبدّلوا); (الواو) a conjunction; (لا تأكلوا) like لا تتبدّلوا; (أموالهم) like the first; (إلى أموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from أموالهم «[Note: It may be attached to the verb تأكلوا, on the basis that it includes the meaning of تضمّوا (add) or تجمعوا (gather).]», i.e. added to your wealth, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of inna, referring to the forbidden exchanging and consuming; (كان) an incomplete past verb, its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa", i.e. this deed; (حوبا) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative; (كبيرا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «آتوا اليتامى ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اتّقوا الله in the previous verse.
The clause «تتبدّلوا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتوا اليتامى.
The clause «تأكلوا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتوا اليتامى.
The clause «إنّه كان..» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كان حوبا..» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(حوبا) the maṣdar (verbal noun) of حاب يحوب, of the pattern (bāb) نصر; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.. There is another maṣdar with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَآتُوا الْيَتامى أَمْوالَهُمْ»: what is meant by giving them their wealth is leaving it intact, not interfering with it harmfully. It is thus a trope used for what its meaning entails, since wealth is only given if it is in that state. The subtle point (nukta) in this expression is the indication that the aim of refraining from interfering should be the delivery of the wealth to those mentioned, not merely refraining from interfering with it. On this basis it is valid that by اليتامى the young are meant, as is the immediate sense, and the command is specific to the guardians and executors who manage their affairs.
If what is meant is giving the wealth to those who have reached the age of maturity after having been orphans, then the word «يتامى» here is a mursal (non-metaphorical) trope (majāz mursal), because it is used for the mature.
The relation is regard for what they formerly were.
2- «وَلا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوالَهُمْ»: an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya):
He likened their wealth to food that is eaten, then borrowed for it the most prominent property of food, namely eating. In this metaphor lies one of the subtlest secrets:
The masters of rhetoric (ahl al-bayān) say: when what is forbidden has degrees, the way of eloquence is to forbid the lowest of them, as a pointer to the highest, as in the saying of the Exalted: «فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ». If you test this rule against this verse, you find it at first sight contrary to it, since the highest degree of consuming an orphan's wealth, in terms of prohibition, is that one consumes it while having no need of it, and the lowest that one consumes it while in need of it. The requirement of the stated rule would then be to forbid one who is in need from consuming the orphan's wealth, so that the prohibition of the one without need follows a fortiori. There is no doubt that forbidding the lowest, even though it conveys the prohibition of the highest, still leaves forbidding the highest another great benefit not obtained from forbidding the lowest: the more hideous the forbidden thing, the more the soul is repelled by it and the more remote the motive towards it. There is no doubt that what is settled in souls is that consuming an orphan's wealth while having no need of it is the most hideous form of consuming, so it was singled out for prohibition to denounce whoever falls into it.
4- «[Translator's note: so numbered in the source; there is no point 3.]» Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): between الخبيث, which is unlawful wealth, and الطيب, which is lawful and acceptable.

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (خفتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) a pronoun, the fāʿil (agent); (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (لا) negative; (تقسطوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent; (في اليتامى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تقسطوا), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddara) on the alif, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. in marrying the orphan girls «[Note: The verse was revealed concerning the guardians of orphans.]».
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تقسطوا ...) is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object)..
(الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (انكحوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, direct object «[Note: (ما) is used here for women — who are rational beings — because it applies to the kind, i.e. so marry the kind that is pleasing to you among women.]»; (طاب) a past verb, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa", and it is the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid); (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (طاب); (من النساء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in طاب «[Note: They are the women not related to them, other than the orphan girls.]»; (مثنى) a ḥāl, accusative, from ما «[Note: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: a ḥāl from النساء, and that is weak in the view of Abū Ḥayyān.]», the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif; it is prevented from taking tanwīn because of the two causes of being an adjective and of deflection (al-ʿadl); (الواو) a conjunction for choice (takhyīr); (ثلاث) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to مثنى, accusative, a diptote; (رباع) like ثلاث, accusative; (الفاء) a conjunction; (إن خفتم ألّا تعدلوا) like خفتم ألّا تقسطوا; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (واحدة) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "انكحوا" (marry); (أو) a conjunction for choice; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, conjoined to واحدة «[Note: See footnote no. (1) above; (ما) here is like that one.]»; (ملكت) a past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine; (أيمان) the agent, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).. (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the reference is to marrying four, or one, or taking concubines; the (اللام) is for distance and the (الكاف) for address; (أدنى) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (لا) negative; (تعولوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent.
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تعدلوا) «[Translator's note: so in the source; the maṣdar meant here is ألّا تعولوا.]» is in the position of a genitive governed by an omitted preposition, its implied form being إلى أن or لأن, attached to أدنى.
The clause «إن خفتم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تقسطوا..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «انكحوا ...» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «طاب لكم..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «إن خفتم (the second)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن خفتم (the first).
The clause «(انكحوا) واحدة» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ملكت أيمانكم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «ذلك أدنى..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا تعولوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(طاب) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion (qalb); its original is طيب: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif..
(مثنى) a derived adjective on the wazn مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; it is deflected (maʿdūl) from another expression, namely اثنتان اثنتان or ثنتان ثنتان (two by two).
(ثلاث) a derived adjective on the wazn فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ.. it is deflected from another expression, namely ثلاث ثلاث with fatḥa on the thāʾ (three by three).
(رباع) like ثلاث.
(تعولوا) its past is عال, of the pattern (bāb) نصر, and it means "to be unjust" (جار).

* Rhetoric:
1- فَانْكِحُوا ما طابَ لَكُمْ»: in this verse is the device of predominance (al-taghlīb).
«ما» was preferred over «من» in order to refer to the description, e.g. virgin or previously married. «ما» is specific — or predominant — for non-rational beings when the essence is intended; but when the description is intended, it is not, as when you say: ما زيد؟ in a question, i.e. is he virtuous or generous?
And «أكرم ما شئت من الرجال» (honour whatever you wish of men), meaning the generous or the base.

* Benefits:
1- The rule is that «من» is for rational beings and «ما» for non-rational beings, but there is latitude for each of them. In this verse «ما» has been used for rational beings, contrary to the rule. The grammarians hold that this is infrequent, and more frequent when rational beings are joined with non-rational beings in one ruling, as in His saying, Glorified be He: «يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ»; under this ruling fall both what is rational and what is not, alike..
2- Lifting injustice from the orphan girl.
It was the custom of the Arabs in the Jāhiliyya that the guardian of an orphan girl would withhold her from others if she was beautiful and wealthy, and marry her himself, though she might be unwilling. Allah wished to free her from this hateful wrong, so He revealed this verse.
3- It is stated in the books of grammar, in the chapter on diptotes, that what is deflected from the numbers one to ten is a diptote, and the reason for the deflection is the repetition of the number; it is said that this form was substituted for repeating the number. As for the cause of its being a diptote, it is said to be «deflection and being an adjective», and it is said to be because of deflection and definiteness by the intention of the omitted alif and lām (al-), owing to the intention of annexation.
There is a view that the two causes are deflection from repetition and the feminine.
Deflection is not permissible unless a plural precedes it, as in جاء القوم مثنى وثلاث ورباع (the people came two by two, three by three and four by four).
There is a disagreement whose gist is: does deflection cover the numbers from one to ten, or is it restricted to what occurs in the Noble Qur'an only, namely مثنى, ثلاث and رباع?
Whoever wishes for more should turn to Mughnī al-Labīb, for in it there is sufficiency for one parched with burning thirst.

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(ألم تر إلى الذين): its i'rab has already been given «[Note: In verse (44) of this sūra.]»; (يزكّون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) …, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أنفس) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) away from their purifying themselves, and of a new beginning; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (يزكي) is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; (يشاء) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is «هو»; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; (يظلمون) is an imperfect verb, passive, nominative …, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (فتيلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its description, i.e. «ظلما قدر الفتيل», accusative.
The clause «لم تر إلى الذين …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يزكون …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «الله يزكي …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يزكّي …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(يزكون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its original form is يزكّيون with ḍamma on the second yāʾ; its vowel was transferred to the kāf, then it was dropped because of the two sukūns. (الفتيل): a derived noun, its pattern being فعيل in the sense of مفعول, if its meaning is taken as that which is twisted …; and it is a (non-derived) noun if it denotes the long line in the cleft of a date-stone.

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(انظر) is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (كيف) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (يفترون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (على الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يفترون) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of الكذب.]»; (الكذب) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) «[Note: Since fabrication (iftirāʾ) coincides with lying in meaning, or is close to it, it is permissible to parse (الكذب) as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its synonym.]»; (الواو) is resumptive; (كفى) is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الباء) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (الهاء) is in the position of genitive in the near position and in the position of nominative as the fāʿil in the remote position; (إثما) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative «[Note: Or a ḥāl, accusative.]»; (مبينا) is a naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «انظر …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يفترون …» is in the position of accusative as the object of انظر, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «كفى به إثما …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:51-55.t:
* I'rab:
(ألم تر … من الكتاب): its i'rab has already been given «[Note: In verse (44) of this sūra.]»; (يؤمنون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn …, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent); (بالجبت) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يؤمنون); (الواو) is a conjunction; (الطاغوت) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الجبت, genitive like it; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يقولون) is like يؤمنون; (اللام) is a preposition; (الذين) is a relative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (يقولون); (كفروا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (ها) is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (أولاء) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أهدى) is the khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (من الذين) is like للذين, attached to أهدى; (آمنوا) is like كفروا; (سبيلا) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb), governed by أهدى.
The clause «لم تر إلى الذين …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أوتوا نصيبا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يؤمنون …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of أوتوا «[Note: It may be an explanatory resumptive clause (istiʾnāfiyya bayāniyya), as though it were the answer to an implied question.]».
The clause «يقولون …» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يؤمنون.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «هؤلاء أهدى» is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative (الذين).
(52) أولاء is like the first, and (الكاف) is a particle of address; (الذين) is a relative in the position of nominative as the khabar; (لعن) is a past verb and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) is resumptive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (يلعن) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it is given kasra because two sukūns met; (الله) is like the previous; (الفاء) links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لن) is a particle of negation and the accusative; (تجد) is an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (اللام) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (نصيرا), which is the second object of the verb تجد; as for the first, it is implied, i.e. «أحدا».
The clause «أولئك الذين …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لعنهم الله» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يلعن الله» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لن تجد …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
(53) (أم) is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of «بل» and the hamza; (لهم) is like له, attached to a fronted khabar; (نصيب) is a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (من الملك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of نصيب; (الفاء) occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition; (إذا), with tanwīn, is a particle of response with no position; (لا) is negating; (يؤتون) is an imperfect verb, nominative …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الناس) is a first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (نقيرا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «لهم نصيب» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يؤتون …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «هم» … and the nominal clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied non-jussive condition «[Note: The implied form is: «إذا أعطوا الملك فهم لا يؤتون الناس نقيرا».]».
(54) (أم) is like the first; (يحسدون) is like يؤمنون; (الناس) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (على) is a preposition; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (يحسدون); (آتاهم) is like لعنهم; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (من فضل) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the implied resumptive pronoun (ʿāʾid) of the relative «[Note: I.e.: «ما آتاهم إيّاه الله من فضله».]», and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) is causal (taʿlīliyya); (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (آتينا) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn …, and (نا) is a pronoun, the fāʿil; (آل) is a first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (إبراهيم) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (الكتاب) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (الحكمة) is conjoined to الكتاب, accusative like it; (الواو) is a conjunction; (آتينا) is like the first, and (هم) is a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (ملكا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (عظيما) is a naʿt, accusative.
The clause «يحسدون الناس» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آتاهم الله» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «آتينا آل إبراهيم …» has no grammatical position, causal.
The clause «آتيناهم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the causal clause.
(55) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (منهم) is like لهم «1»; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ; (آمن) is a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو», and it is the resumptive pronoun; (به) is like له, attached to (آمن); (الواو) is a conjunction; (منهم من صدّ عنه) is like منهم من آمن به; (الواو) is resumptive; (كفى بجهنّم سعيرا) is like كفى به إثما «2».
The clause «منهم من آمن …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يحسدون.
The clause «آمن به» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first relative (من).
The clause «منهم من صدّ عنه» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause منهم من آمن.
The clause «صد عنه» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «كفى بجهنم …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الجبت): a noun for whatever is worshipped besides Allah, whether an idol or something else; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn.
(أهدى): a noun of preference (ism tafḍīl) from هدى يهدي, of the bāb of ضرب; its pattern is أفعل, and it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion: its original form is أهدي — with yāʾ —; when the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa it was converted into an alif, and it is written in the form of a yāʾ because it is the fourth letter.
(نقيرا): it is فعيل in the sense of مفعول, either meaning the small pit on the back of a date-stone, or what is engraved in stone or wood.

* Benefits:
1- The view of the grammarians on «إذن».
The grammarians hold many views about it, which we summarise as follows:
a- It comes as a particle that puts the imperfect verb in the accusative, on condition that nothing separates it from the verb in the accusative except «the oath», as in the poet's saying:
إذن والله نرميهم بحرب ... تشيب الطفل من قبل المشيب
(Then, by Allah, we shall strike them with a war … that turns the child grey before the age of greyness.)
b- If it is preceded by wāw or fāʾ: if we consider the wāw and fāʾ as conjunctions, it is cancelled and the verb after it follows the verb before it. But if we consider the speech a fresh start free of conjunction, it is operative and the verb after it is accusative.
c- If it is preceded by a governor before it, it is made inoperative and the governor takes precedence over it, as in your saying: «إن تذهب إذن أذهب معك».
d- The preferred view is that it be written with nūn and not with alif, and there is detail on that.

safi-cedvel:159-159.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إن) negating (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, which is a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «ما أحد من أهل الكتاب» (there is no one of the People of the Book) (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (إلّا) particle of restriction (اللام) the lām of the oath (يؤمننّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative.. and (النون) the nūn of emphasis, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he) (الباء) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يؤمننّ), (قبل) adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يؤمننّ), (موت) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) resumptive (يوم) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (شهيدا), (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (يكون) defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the noun of يكون is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", referring to ʿĪsā (Jesus), peace be upon him; and it is said that it refers to the Messenger ﷺ (على) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (شهيدا), which is the khabar (predicate) of يكون, accusative.
The clause «إن (أحد) من أهل ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يؤمننّ به»: has no grammatical position, the answer to an implied oath; and the clause of the oath together with its answer is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «يكون عليهم شهيدا»: has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the resumptive nominal clause.].

safi-cedvel:160-161.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction (بظلم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (حرّمنا), (من) preposition (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of ظلم (هادوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (حرّمنا) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) is the fāʿil (عليهم) dealt with in the previous verse, attached to (حرّمنا), (طيّبات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra (أحلّت) passive past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya" (it) (اللام) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أحلّت), (الواو) conjunction (بصدّهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (حرّمنا), (عن سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) صدّ (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (كثيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar, its governor being صدّ [Note: or standing in for an adverb; and it may also be parsed as the object of الصدّ, because it is the qualifier of the object, i.e. «بصدّهم ناسا كثيرا» (by their turning many people away).], and the object of the maṣdar صدّ is omitted, its implied form being: الناس (people) (الواو) conjunction (أخذهم) like صدّهم, and conjoined to it (الربا) mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar أخذ, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq) (نهوا) passive past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (عن) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (نهوا), (الواو) conjunction (أكلهم أموال) like أخذهم الربا, and conjoined to it (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (بالباطل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the third-person pronoun in أكلهم, i.e. «متلبسين بالباطل» (engaged in falsehood) [Note: it may be attached to the maṣdar (أكل), the bāʾ being causal.], (الواو) conjunction (أعتدنا) past verb and its fāʿil (للكافرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعتدنا), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (منهم) like لهم, attached to a ḥāl of الكافرين (عذابا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أليما) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «حرّمنا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied clause (لعنّاهم) [Note: in verse (155) of this surah.].
The clause «هادوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أحلّت لهم»: in the position of accusative, a naʿt of طيّبات.
The clause «قد نهوا ...»: in the position of accusative, a ḥāl.
The clause «أعتدنا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause حرّمنا.

* Rhetoric:
Ibhām (deliberate vagueness): in His saying, Exalted is He, «فبظلم»; and referring to them by this title signals the utter enormity of their wrongdoing, by recalling that it occurred after that tremendous repentance, following the indication of its magnitude through the tanwīn of magnification, i.e. because of a great wrongdoing, beyond the bounds of [similar] things and counterparts, issuing from them.

safi-cedvel:85-85.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يشفع) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (شفاعة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (حسنة) naʿt (adjective), accusative; (يكن) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of يكن [Note: Or attached to (يكن) as a complete verb.] , (نصيب) the noun of يكن, nominative [Note: Or the fāʿil of the complete يكن.
(3, 4) The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.] , (من) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of نصيب; (الواو) conjunction; (من يشفع ... كفل منها) like its counterpart above. (الواو) resumptive; (كان) an incomplete past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of كان, nominative; (على كل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (مقيتا); (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (مقيتا) the khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «من يشفع ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يشفع شفاعة ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «3» .
The clause «يكن له نصيب» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «من يشفع (the second)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يشفع (the second)» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من) «4» .
The clause «يكن له كفل [Note: It is borrowed from the كفل of the camel, which is a cloth wrapped around its hump so that one may ride on it; it was called كفل because it does not cover the whole back but only a portion of it (al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ of Abū Ḥayyān).]» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «كان الله ... مقيتا» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(كفل): a noun meaning a double share of the reward, or meaning a portion; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.
(مقيتا): an active participle from the four-letter أقات, meaning "to have power over it" ... The word contains iʿlāl (phonological change) following the iʿlāl of the verb originally, which the active participle then followed. The imperfect of أقات is يقيت, whose origin is يقوت; the kasra was heavy on the wāw, so it was made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the qāf before it — this is iʿlāl by making quiescent — then the wāw was converted into a yāʾ because it was quiescent and preceded by a kasra — this is iʿlāl by conversion — and the same iʿlāl took place in مقيت.

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إذا) an adverb for future time containing the sense of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis; (حييتم) a passive past verb, indeclinable on sukūn ... and (تم) a pronoun, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (بتحية) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (حييتم); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (حيّوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بأحسن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (حيوا); the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, since it is a diptote because of being descriptive and of the pattern أفعل; (من) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to أحسن; (أو) a conjunction; (ردوا) like حيوا, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (كان على كل شيء حسيبا) like كان على كل شيء مقيتا [Note: in the previous verse (85).] .
The clause «حيّيتم ...» is in the position of genitive through the annexation of (إذا) to it.
The clause «حيّوا ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ردّوها» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «إنّ الله كان ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive, containing the sense of giving the reason.
The clause «كان ... حسيبا» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(تحية): a regular maṣdar (verbal noun) of the four-letter verb حيّا; the tāʾ is a compensation for the yāʾ of تفعيل. The origin of the word is تحيية, of the pattern of تزكية; the kasra was heavy on the first yāʾ, so it was transferred to the ḥāʾ, then the two yāʾs were assimilated together because the first was quiescent.
(حيّوا): it contains iʿlāl (phonological change) by deletion; its origin is حييوا; the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so its vowel was transferred to what precedes it, then it was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters — the sukūn of the yāʾ and the sukūn of the wāw of the plural — so it became حيّوا, of the pattern فعّوا with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
Greeting in Islam:
1- Islam made its greeting: «السلام عليكم» or «السلام عليكم ورحمة الله» or «السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته» .. Replying to it with something better is by adding to each of them — except the third, since no addition remains for one seeking more — so the third is returned with its like; this is how it is reported from the Prophet ﷺ.
In this verse we perceive the constant endeavour to strengthen the ties of affection and kinship among the members of society; spreading the greeting of peace, and replying to the greeting with something better, are among the best means of establishing these ties and strengthening them.
Spreading the greeting of peace is a sunna, while replying to it is an obligation by the ruling of this verse.
Perhaps the purpose of the Quran in placing this verse in the midst of the verses of fighting is to point to the fundamental principle of Islam ... peace.. for Islam is the religion of peace.
2- The saying of Allah the Exalted: فَحَيُّوا بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْها — بأحسن is a preposition and its genitive noun, and the sign of its genitive is the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a diptote. The reason it is a diptote is that it is an adjective of the pattern أفعل. The diptote takes the fatḥa in the genitive in place of the kasra on condition that it is not in annexation (muḍāf), as in مررت بأحسن الناس, and not made definite with (ال), as in مررت بالأحسن خلقا.

safi-cedvel:87-87.t:
* I'rab:
(الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (إله) the noun of لا, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative; (إلا) a particle of exception; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) of the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar (predicate), its implied form being "موجود" ("existing"); (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (يجمعنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of nominative ... and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (إلى يوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يجمعنّكم), by making it include the sense of يحشرنّكم ("He will surely gather you"); (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (لا ريب) like لا إله; (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the khabar of لا; (الواو) resumptive; (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أصدق) khabar, nominative; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أصدق; (حديثا) tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «الله لا إله إلا هو» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا إله إلا هو» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «يجمعنكم ...» has no grammatical position, the reply to an implied oath.
The clause «لا ريب فيه» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of يوم القيامة.
The clause «من أصدق ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:88-88.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of ما; (في المنافقين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of فئتين, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (فئتين) ḥāl of the pronoun of address in (لكم), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أركس) a past verb and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive.. and the clause is its ṣila (relative clause).] (كسبوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation; (تريدون) an imperfect verb, nominative ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (تهدوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (أضلّ) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative, and the object is omitted.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تهدوا ...) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being تريدون.
(الواو) resumptive; (من) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (يضلل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لن) a particle of negation and the subjunctive; (تجد) an imperfect verb, subjunctive; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta"; (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تجد); (سبيلا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «ما لكم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «الله أركسهم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «أركسهم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «كسبوا» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تريدون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تهدوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «أضل الله» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «يضلل الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لن تجد له سبيلا» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with al-fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:162-162.t:
* I'rab:
