(لكن) particle of istidrāk (rectification), with no governing effect, and it was given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters (الراسخون) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw (في العلم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (الراسخون), (من) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الراسخون), (الواو) conjunction (المؤمنون) conjoined to (الراسخون), nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (يؤمنون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (الباء) preposition (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (يؤمنون), (أنزل) passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (it) (إلى) preposition and (الكاف) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل), (الواو) conjunction (ما أنزل) like the first, and conjoined to it (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the second (أنزل), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (المقيمين) a noun in the accusative by way of praise (madḥ), by an omitted verb, its implied form being "أمدح" (I praise) [Note: there are other views on accounting for المقيمين, namely: a- it is conjoined to the relative noun (بما أنزل), genitive like it; b- it is conjoined to the kāf in His saying (إليك) .. or in His saying (من قبلك), i.e.: «أنزل إلى إليك وإلى المقيمين الصلاة» [Translator's note: the source has «إلى إليك» here, apparently a misprint for «إليك»] (it was sent down to you and to those who establish the prayer).. or «من قبلك ومن قبل المقيمين الصلاة» (before you and before those who establish the prayer).], (الصلاة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle المقيمين (الواو) conjunction (المؤتون) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" (they), and it has been cut off from what precedes it, also for praise; nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (الزكاة) mafʿūl bihi of the active participle (المؤتون), accusative (manṣūb) (الواو) conjunction (المؤمنون) conjoined to (المؤتون), nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the active participle (المؤمنون), (الواو) conjunction (اليوم) conjoined to the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr) like it (الآخر) naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, genitive, (أولئك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) is for address (السين) particle of the future (نؤتي) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu" (We), for majesty, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (أجرا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (عظيما) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «الراسخون ... يؤمنون»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يؤمنون ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ [Note: the clause may be a ḥāl of (الراسخون) and what is conjoined to it.. with the clause «أولئك سنؤتيهم..» being the khabar of (الراسخون); this is a weak account, rejected by Abū Ḥayyān, because cutting off a qualifier for praise usually comes at the completion of the utterance, not within it.].
The clause «أنزل إليك»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «أنزل من قبلك»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «(أمدح) المقيمين ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «(هم) المؤتون ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أمدح المقيمين.
The clause «أولئك سنؤتيهم ...»: has no grammatical position, explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya bayāniyya).
The clause «سنؤتيهم ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).

* Benefits:
1- His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿لكِنِ الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ مِنْهُمْ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾. In this verse we are dealing with لكن, which is the lightened form of the heavy (لكنّ); the majority hold that لكنّ, which governs as إنّ governs, becomes a particle of istidrāk (rectification) when lightened. But we will speak about it in some detail, presenting some of the views of the grammarians in this area:
1- لكن lightened from the heavy [form] is a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ) conveying istidrāk, and it does not govern. So in the verse above, الراسخون is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يؤمنون is its khabar (predicate). However, some grammarians, such as al-Akhfash and Yūnus, permitted it to govern.
2- If a resumed utterance comes after it, it is a particle of commencement conveying istidrāk, not a conjunction; it may be used with the wāw, as in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَما ظَلَمْناهُمْ وَلكِنْ كانُوا هُمُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾, and without it, as in the saying of Zuhayr:
إن ابن ورقاء لا تخشى بوادره ... لكن وقائعه في الحرب تنتظر
(Ibn Warqāʾ's outbursts are not to be feared, but his onslaughts in war are awaited.)
Ibn Abī al-Rabīʿ claimed that when it is joined with the wāw it conjoins a clause to a clause, and that this is the apparent meaning of Sībawayh's statement; but the more likely view is that the wāw is resumptive and it [لكن] is a particle of istidrāk.
3- If a single word (mufrad) follows it, it is a conjunction under two conditions: the first is that it be preceded by a negation or a prohibition, as in:
ما قام زيد لكن عمرو (Zayd did not stand, but ʿAmr [did]), and لا يقم زيد لكن عمرو (let Zayd not stand, but ʿAmr). If you say قام زيد (Zayd stood) and then bring لكن, you make it a particle of commencement and bring a clause, saying لكن عمرو لم يقم (but ʿAmr did not stand). The Kufans permitted لكن عمرو as a conjunction, but this is not attested (masmūʿ). The second condition: that it not be joined with the wāw. This was stated by al-Fārisī and most grammarians. Some said: it is not used with a single word except with the wāw; but the stronger view is the first, namely that it is not joined with the wāw, because that suits the eloquent Arabic style.
2- His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ﴾: it has been observed in this verse that المقيمين differs from what precedes it in i'rab, namely in being accusative, although what precedes it is nominative. The views of the grammarians and the exegetes on this topic have diverged, and we will present a selection of them.
1- The majority of the Quran readers read it in the accusative, and this word has been parsed as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being أعني (I mean) and أخصّ (I single out); this is the school of the Basrans.
2- Some people of short understanding, who do not know the ways of the Arabs and their manners of expression, claimed that this is an error that occurred in the Muṣḥaf, as if the eminent masters of learning had been heedless of it. Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn Jarīr replied to this claim and refuted the claim of those people, and showed that this is a genuine Arabic style, namely the accusative of specification (al-naṣb ʿalā al-ikhtiṣāṣ), and that the first forerunners among the noble Companions, among them the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, were of such soundness of Arabic instinct and eloquence that something like this could not escape them. Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn Jarīr cited evidence from poetry of this pattern, namely the saying of the poet:
لا يبعدن قومي الذين هم ... أسد العداة وآفة الجزر

النازلين بكل معترك ... والطيبون معاقد الأزر
(May my people never perish, who are lions against enemies and the bane of slaughter-camels; / those who alight in every battlefield, and those pure at the tying of the waist-wrappers.)
The point of evidence: his saying «النازلين», where it would have to be nominative if it were a qualifier of what precedes it. But the poet put it in the accusative by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), and when he conjoined what follows it, he did not conjoin it to it, but conjoined it to what precedes it, in the nominative.
- There are other accounts by the grammarians of this word that there is no need to present; but we say that the rules of Arabic were derived from the Noble Quran, the noble Hadith, and the sayings of the Arabs in poetry and prose, and that these rules have not encompassed all the states of the Arabs' speech; rather they fall short, because the language is too vast to be encompassed by rules. We make the Noble Quran the judge over the rules, and we do not make the rules a judge over the Noble Quran, as the scholars of the foundations of grammar (uṣūl al-naḥw) have established.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (آتوا) like انكحوا in the previous verse; (النساء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (صدقات) a second direct object, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (هنّ) an attached pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (نحلة) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the agent pronoun, i.e. giving freely (nāḥilīn), or from النساء, i.e. given freely (manḥūlāt) «[Note: Or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it meets it in derivation, i.e. أنحلوهن صدقاتهنّ نحلة (give them their dowries as a free gift).]». (الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (طبن) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (النون) a pronoun, the fāʿil (agent); (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (طبن), by making it include the meaning of تنازلن (they relinquish); (عن شيء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (طبن); (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of شيء; (نفسا) a tamyīz (specification), accusative, transformed from the agent; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (كلوا) like انكحوا in the previous verse, and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object; (هنيئا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar because it is its qualifier, i.e. أكلا هنيئا (a wholesome eating); and likewise مريئا.]», either from the wāw, i.e. enjoying it (hāniʾīn), or from the hāʾ, i.e. made wholesome (muhannaʾan); (مريئا) likewise a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl.
The clause «آتوا النساء..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the first resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «إن طبن لكم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كلوه هنيئا» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(صدقاتهنّ) plural of صدقة, a noun for the dowry (mahr); its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa then ḍamma. There are other nouns for the dowry: صدقة with two fatḥas, and with fatḥa then sukūn, and صداق with fatḥa on the ṣād and with kasra.
(نحلة) a hearsay-based (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb نحلتها أنحلها, of the pattern (bāb) فتح, i.e. I gave her the dowry; its wazn is فعلة with kasra on the fāʾ.
(طبن) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion suited to being indeclinable on sukūn, because it is a hollow weak verb. Its original is طيبن; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted to escape the meeting of two quiescent letters. Its wazn is فلن with kasra then sukūn.
(هنيئا) the prevailing view about this word is that it is derived from هنؤ يهنؤ, of the pattern كرم, on the wazn فعيل. al-ʿUkbarī said: it is a maṣdar that came on the wazn فعيل.
(مريئا) its derivation matches the derivation of (هنيئا), so it is like it; its verb is مرأ يمرأ, of the pattern فتح; مرئ يمرأ, of the pattern فرح; and مرؤ يمرؤ, of the pattern كرم.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā, jussive-governing; (تؤتوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (السفهاء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (أموال) a second direct object, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, naʿt (adjective) of أموال; (جعل) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, agent, nominative (marfūʿ); the omitted returning pronoun is the first direct object, i.e. جعلها (made it); (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (قياما) — a naʿt placed before the noun it qualifies —; (قياما) a second direct object, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (ارزقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent; (وهم) «[Translator's note: so in the source, «وهم»; the pronoun هم is meant.]» a pronoun, direct object; (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (ارزقوهم), i.e. from it; (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (اكسوا، قولوا) like ارزقوا, and (هم) the third-person pronoun, direct object; (لهم) like لكم, attached to (قولوا); (قولا) a direct object, accusative; (معروفا) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «لا تؤتوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتوا النساء in the previous verse.
The clause «جعل الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «ارزقوهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا تؤتوا ...
The clause «اكسوهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ارزقوهم.
The clause «قولوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ارزقوهم.

* Morphology:
(تؤتوا) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion and a change by vowel-removal (taskīn). Its original is تؤتيوا: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the tāʾ; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted to escape the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(السفهاء) plural of سفيه, an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha); its wazn is فعيل. (See verse 13 of Sūrat al-Baqara, and 282 of Sūrat al-Baqara.)
(اكسوهم) it contains a weak-letter change by deletion; its original is اكسووهم or اكسيوهم. The vowel on the weak letter, the final radical (lām) of the verb, was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent and the vowel of the letter was transferred to the letter before it.. then the weak letter was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (ابتلوا) like ارزقوا «[Note: in the previous verse.]»; (اليتامى) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif; (حتّى) a particle of commencement (ibtidāʾ); (إذا) an adverb of future time including the meaning of a condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis «[Note: i.e.: when they reach marriageable age, being of sound judgement, then hand over ...]»; (بلغوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (النكاح) a direct object, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of إذا; (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (آنستم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... and (تم) a pronoun, the agent; (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (آنستم); (رشدا) a direct object, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of إن; (ادفعوا) like ابتلوا; (إليهم) like منهم, attached to (ادفعوا); (أموال) a direct object, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā, jussive-governing; (تأكلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and (ها) a direct object; (إسرافا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) «[Note: Or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and likewise (بدارا).]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (بدارا) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (إسرافا), accusative like it; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يكبروا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the agent.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكبروا) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object governed by the maṣdar بدار «[Note: Or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. for fear that they grow up.]», i.e. hastening [to anticipate] their growing up, that is, hurrying to squander it before they grow up.
(الواو) resumptive; (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (كان) an incomplete past verb, in the position of a jussive, the protasis, its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa", referring to من; (غنيّا) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اللام) the jussive-governing lām of command; (يستعفف) an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command, and the agent is "huwa"; (الواو) a conjunction; (من ... فليأكل) like من كان غنيّا فليستعفف; (بالمعروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of يأكل, i.e. being fair «[Note: The preposition may be attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: أكلا بالمعروف (an eating in a fair manner).]»; (الفاء) resumptive; (إذا دفعتم) like إذا بلغوا; (إليهم) like the first, attached to (دفعتم); (أموالهم) its i'rab has passed in the verse «[Translator's note: the verse number is missing in the source.]»; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (أشهدوا) like ابتلوا; (عليهم) like إليهم, attached to (أشهدوا); (الواو) resumptive; (كفى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif; (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (الله) the Name of Majesty, genitive in form, nominative in position, the agent of كفى; (حسيبا) a ḥāl, accusative «[Note: Or a tamyīz (specification), accusative.]».
The clause «ابتلوا اليتامى» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an earlier resumption.
The clause «بلغوا ...» is in the position of a genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إن آنستم..» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of إذا.
The clause «ادفعوا ...» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis of إن, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا تأكلوها ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ابتلوا «[Note: Or it is resumptive, and this is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān ... He said: "This clause is independent ... and is not conjoined to the apodosis of the condition, because the condition is consequent upon reaching marriageable age, and that conflicts with His saying وبدارا أن يكبروا ... By this the error of whoever made (ولا تأكلوها) conjoined to (فادفعوا) becomes clear ..." End quote.]».
The clause «يكبروا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative.
The clause «من كان غنيّا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان غنيّا ...» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «1» «[Translator's note: the footnote markers «1» and «2» appear in the source without accompanying footnote text.]».
The clause «ليستعفف» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «من كان فقيرا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من كان غنيّا.
The clause «كان فقيرا» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من) «2».
The clause «ليأكل بالمعروف» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «دفعتم ...» is in the position of a genitive, by the annexation of (إذا) to it.
The clause «أشهدوا عليهم» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «كفي بالله حسيبا» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(بدارا) a hearsay-based (samāʿī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb بادر; the regular (qiyāsī) one is مبادرة. Its wazn is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(حسيبا) an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) of the verb حسب يحسب, of the pattern (bāb) نصر; its wazn is فعيل, and it means the one who takes account (al-muḥāsib).

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَمَنْ كانَ غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ»: in this verse is one of the delightful kinds of rhetoric called «strength of wording for strength of meaning», and that is in His saying «فليستعفف».
For «استعفّ» is more eloquent than «عف», as though he seeks an increase of chastity from himself, humbling it and holding it to integrity.

* Benefits:
1- Part of the social legislation: these two verses urge preserving the wealth of orphans, and explain when the executor in charge of the orphan may benefit, through his supervision and management, from the orphan's wealth in his possession,
and when he must keep himself chaste and refrain scrupulously from approaching it, and consequently when the executor must hand over the orphan's wealth to him, and the obligation of taking witnesses to that.
Thus we find Islam always standing by the weak so that he becomes strong, and by the one who has a right so that he obtains his right.
2- «كفى» has three meanings: the first is to emphasise sufficiency and exaggerate it.
The second is in the sense of «أجزأ» (to be adequate), and the third in the sense of «وقى» (to protect).
As for the first, the bāʾ often enters upon its agent and seldom upon its object, as in the verse mentioned above, and as in the poet's saying:
كفي بجسمي نحولا أنني رجل ... لولا مخاطبتي إياك لم ترني
(It suffices as thinness of my body that I am a man whom, were it not for my speaking to you, you would not see.)
As for the second and third, the bāʾ may not enter upon their agent or their object; so reflect.
(3) The fāʾ linking the apodosis: it enters upon the apodosis of a condition, whether it is the apodosis of a jussive-governing condition or of a non-jussive condition. If it is the first, the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; if the second, the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
It also enters upon the apodosis of the condition when it is an imperfect verb, and in this case the lām of command must precede the verb, as in the saying of the Exalted: «وَمَنْ كانَ غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ»; the verb is then jussive by «the lām of command», and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis.

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters); (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (كفروا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بآيات) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (كفروا), and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (سوف) is a particle of futurity; (نصلي) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (هم) is a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is «نحن», for majesty; (نارا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (كلما) is an adverb of time, accusative, carrying the meaning of the condition, attached to (بدّلناهم) …, and ما is a maṣdar-forming particle «[Note: It is permissible to parse (كلّما) as one word, an adverb of time carrying the meaning of the condition, attached to (بدّلنا).]»; (نضجت) is a past verb …, and (التاء) is for the feminine; (جلود) is the fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما نضجت جلودهم) is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
(بدّلنا) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn …, and (نا) is the fāʿil, and (هم) is a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi, and it is on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «بدّلنا جلودهم» «[Note: Or there is something implied, namely the preposition and its genitive noun, i.e. «بدلناهم بجلودهم جلودا غيرها», so that the omitted bāʾ is supplied.]»; (جلودا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (غير) is a naʿt (adjective) of جلود, accusative like it, and (ها) is a muḍāf ilayhi; (اللام) is the lām of causation (taʿlīl); (يذوقوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an «أن» concealed after the lām of causation, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (العذاب) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يذوقوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (بدّلناهم).
(إنّ) is like the first; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (كان) is a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (عزيزا) is the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative; (حكيما) is a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «إنّ الذين كفروا …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «سوف نصليهم …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «نضجت جلودهم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «بدّلناهم …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يذوقوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ الله كان …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كان عزيزا …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
Istiʿāra makniyya (implicit metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: لِيَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ.
Expressing the perception of the punishment by tasting, in that it suffers no diminution through continued contact; or to convey the bitterness of the punishment together with its painfulness; or to draw attention to the intensity of its effect, in that the faculty of taste is the most affecting of the senses. The thing to which it is likened was omitted, and one of its concomitants, namely tasting, was borrowed.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted: كُلَّما نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بَدَّلْناهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَها لِيَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ — «كلما» is one of the non-jussive conditional particles, which are: «إذا، لو، لولا، كلما»; it conveys the meaning of condition and of adverbial time, and the clause after it is in the position of genitive by annexation. It is required that its protasis and its own apodosis come in the past form and nothing else.
It is fitting to point out, concerning this verse, that among the artistic inimitability of the Qurʾān is that it presents ideas embodied within a frame of movement and life, so that sense, imagination, thought and feeling contemplate them at length, as though they were a living reality visible before the reader or listener.
On hearing this verse we call to mind the images of continual punishment that never ceases, and the skin that hardly ينضح «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «ينضج» (is roasted through)]» before it is renewed, and so on without cessation or end.

safi-cedvel:89-90.t:
* I'rab:
(ودّوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (لو) a maṣdar-forming particle; (تكفرون) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (لو تكفرون) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governing word being ودّوا.
(الكاف) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (كفروا) like ودوا.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كفروا) is in the position of genitive by al-kāf, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. تكفرون كفرا ككفرهم ("you disbelieve with a disbelief like their disbelief").
(الفاء) conjunction; (تكونون) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the noun of تكون; (سواء) khabar (predicate), accusative. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (لا) the prohibitive lā that makes the verb jussive; (تتخذوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a second mafʿūl bihi [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of أولياء, if it is taken as transitive to one object.] , (أولياء) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (حتى) a particle of limit and the genitive; (يهاجروا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى, the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the agent of يهاجروا; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يهاجروا ...) is in the position of genitive by (حتى), attached to (تتخذوا).
(الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (تولوا) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (خذوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (اقتلوهم) like خذوهم; (حيث) an adverb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (اقتلوهم); (وجدتم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn ...
and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil, and (الواو) redundant (zāʾida) to lengthen the vowel of the mīm, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (لا تتخذوا منهم وليّا) like the preceding; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant, to emphasize the negation; (نصيرا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) by al-wāw to (وليّا), accusative like it.
The clause «ودّوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تكفرون» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (لو).
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تكونون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تكفرون.
The clause «لا تتّخذوا ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. إن بانت عداوتهم فلا تتّخذوا ("if their enmity becomes evident, then do not take ...").
The clause «يهاجروا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «تولّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied conditional clause.
The clause «خذوهم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «اقتلوهم» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause خذوهم.
The clause «وجدتموهم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا تتخذوا ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause خذوهم.
(إلّا) a particle of exception; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as excepted from the object pronoun in اقتلوهم [Note: The exception cannot be from the taking of allies, because that is forbidden absolutely.] (يصلون) like تكفرون; (إلى قوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يصلون); (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (بينهم) like بينكم and conjoined to it; (ميثاق) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (أو) a conjunction; (جاؤوا) like ودّوا, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (حصرت) a past verb ...
and (التاء) the tāʾ of the feminine; (صدور) fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يقاتلوا) like يهاجروا, and (كم) mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقاتلوكم) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being عن أن يقاتلوكم, attached to (حصرت).
(أو) a conjunction; (يقاتلوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, conjoined to يقاتلوكم ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (قوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) resumptive; (لو) a non-jussive conditional; (شاء) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو; (سلّط) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa", and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (سلّطهم); (الفاء) conjunction; (اللام) to emphasize the link; (قاتلوا) like تولوا, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) conjunction; (إن اعتزلوا) like إن تولوا ... and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) conjunction; (لم) a particle of negation, inversion (of tense) and the jussive; (يقاتلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (ألقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إليكم) like عليكم, attached to (ألقوا); (السلم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (ما) negative; (جعل الله) like شاء الله; (لكم) like عليكم, attached to (جعل) [Note: Or to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb جعل, if it is transitive to two objects.] , (عليهم) like عليكم, attached to a ḥāl of (سبيلا), which is mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «يصلون ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «بينكم ... ميثاق» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.
The clause «جاؤوكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause يصلون.
The clause «حصرت صدورهم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) understood [Note: This clause is performative (inshāʾiyya) in meaning, because it is an imprecation according to al-Mubarrad, so it is resumptive.] , or a naʿt of قوم in the position of genitive.
The clause «يقاتلوكم» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يقاتلوا قومهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle relative.
The clause «لو شاء الله» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «سلّطهم عليكم» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قاتلوكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis.
The clause «اعتزلوكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لو شاء الله.
The clause «لم يقاتلوكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اعتزلوكم.
The clause «ألقوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اعتزلوكم.
The clause «ما جعل الله ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with al-fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(يصلون): it contains iʿlāl (phonological change) by deletion; its fāʾ was deleted, as it is a weak verb of the mithāl type (first radical weak) with kasra on the ʿayn in the imperfect; its pattern is يعلون.
(ألقوا): it contains iʿlāl by deletion; two quiescent letters met, the alif, which is the lām of the word — converted from a yāʾ — and the wāw of the plural, so the alif was deleted and what precedes it was given a fatḥa to indicate it.
(السلم): a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from سالمه, i.e. made peace with him; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Benefits:
1- The saying of Allah the Exalted حَتَّى يُهاجِرُوا — an imperfect verb, subjunctive by the implied أن after حتى, the sign of its subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs. It is worth pointing out the places where the verb is made subjunctive by an implied أن; that is in several places: after حتى, as mentioned; after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: لِتَفْتَرِيَ عَلَيْنا غَيْرَهُ; and after the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهُمْ فَأَفُوزَ فَوْزاً عَظِيماً — and it is known that the fāʾ of causation must be preceded by a wish, a hope, a request or a question; or after (أو) meaning "with", preceded by a maṣdar, as in the saying of Maysūn:
ولبس عباءة وتقرّ عيني ... أحب إليّ من لبس الشفوف
(Wearing a coarse cloak while my eye is content is dearer to me than wearing fine sheer garments.) [Translator's note: in this verse the subjunctive verb follows a conjunctive wāw (و), not أو, although the author cites it under أو.]
and after أو meaning "until", as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فقلت له لا تبك عينك إنما ... نحاول ملكا أو نموت فنعذرا
(So I said to him: let your eye not weep; we only seek a kingdom, or [until] we die and are excused.)
2- The saying of Allah the Exalted: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إِلى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثاقٌ أَوْ جاؤُكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ — opinions have conflicted about the clause (حصرت) in the verse, and we will summarize them as follows.
a- It is an imprecatory clause with no grammatical position, as if Allah were invoking against them that their breasts be constricted.
b- It is in the position of genitive as an adjective of قوم.
c- In the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the wāw of the plural in His saying «جاؤوكم»; the grammarians mention understanding «قد» before a clause functioning as a ḥāl when it is in the past form, i.e. «جاؤوكم قد حصرت» .
d- In the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, the implied form being: أو جاؤوكم قوما حصرت صدورهم ("or come to you as a people whose breasts are constricted").
But we think we should take the matter by the nearest path and not resort to interpretation and artificiality, so as not to leave the general framework of the rules, for they are to help us understand the meaning, not to complicate the meaning ...
3- The saying of Allah the Exalted: أَوْ جاؤُكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ أَنْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ. The interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb يقاتلوكم has three views:
a- Genitive by an implied preposition, i.e. عن أن يقاتلوكم.
b- Accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ).
c- In the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

safi-cedvel:57-57.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (آمنوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and likewise (عملوا); (الصالحات) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (سندخلهم جنّات) is like سوف نصليهم نارا «1», and the sign of the accusative of جنّات is the kasra; (تجري) is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (من تحت) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تجري) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الأنهار.]», and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الأنهار) is the fāʿil, nominative; (خالدين) is a ḥāl, accusative, of the object pronoun in (ندخلهم), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (في) is a preposition and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to خالدين; (أبدا) is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative, attached to خالدين; (لهم) is like فيها, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate), and the second (فيها) is attached to the omitted khabar; (أزواج) is a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (مطهرة) is a naʿt (adjective), nominative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ندخلهم) is like نصليهم «3»; (ظلّا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ظليلا) is a naʿt, accusative.
The clause «الذين آمنوا …» is a clause with no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّ الذين كفروا «4».
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «عملوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «سندخلهم …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «تجري» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of جنّات.
The clause «لهم فيها أزواج» is in the position of accusative as a second naʿt of جنات, or a ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in (سندخلهم).
The clause «ندخلهم …» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause لهم فيها أزواج.

* Morphology:
(ظلّا): a noun from ظلّ يظلّ ظلالة, of the bāb of فتح; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn.
(ظليلا): a derived noun, a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the active participle); its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters); (الله) is the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative (manṣūb); (يأمر) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle; (تؤدّوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الأمانات) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (إلى أهل) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تؤدّوا), and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تؤدّوا) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi «[Note: It may be in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, i.e. «بأن تؤدوا …», attached to (يأمر); see verse (67) of Sūrat al-Baqara.]».
(الواو) is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time carrying the meaning of the condition, attached to an implied (يأمركم); (حكمتم) is a past verb and its fāʿil; (بين) is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative, attached to (حكمتم); (الناس) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (أن تحكموا) is like (أن تؤدوا); (بالعدل) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تحكموا) «[Note: It may be attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of (تحكموا), i.e. «holding fast to justice» or «clothed with it» …]».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تحكموا) is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the implied verb يأمركم.
(إنّ الله) is like the first; (نعم) is a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise, and its fāʿil is a pronoun latent by necessity, its implied form being «هو»; (ما) is a qualified indefinite (nakira mawṣūfa), indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a tamyīz (specification) of the latent pronoun «[Note: (ما) may be a complete definite noun or a relative noun serving as fāʿil, and the clause after it is either an adjective of an omitted qualified noun which is the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ), its implied form being: «نعم الشيء شيء يعظكم …», or it has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, with the makhṣūṣ omitted.]»; (يعظ) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (الباء) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يعظكم); and the one specified for praise is omitted, its implied form being «تأدية الأمانة والحكم بالعدل»; (إنّ الله) is like the first; (كان) is a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (سميعا) is the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative; (بصيرا) is a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «إنّ الله يأمركم …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يأمركم …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the first إنّ.
The clause «تؤدّوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أنّ) «[Translator's note: so in the source, with shadda; the particle in the verse is «أن».]».
The clause «حكمتم …» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The implied clause «يأمركم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تحكموا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ الله نعمّا …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نعمّا يعظكم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the (second) إنّ.
The clause «يعظكم به» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله كان …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كان سميعا …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the (third) إنّ.

* Benefits:
The general trust (amāna):
1- Man alone has been entrusted to his innate nature (fiṭra), his intellect, his will and his effort to reach Allah with help from Him — وَالَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا فِينا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنا — and this is a trust that man has borne and that he must discharge.
From it all other trusts spring forth: the trust of faith in Allah, the trust of dealing with people, the trust of transactions and material deposits, the trust of sincere counsel to the ruler and to the ruled, and the trust of caring for the young.
2- نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ.
«نعمّا» is originally «نعم ما»: the two mīms were assimilated together and became a doubled mīm. نعم is a past verb for expressing praise; as for «ما», there are several schools on its i'rab: The first is that it is a complete definite noun meaning «the thing», and it is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of نعم.
The second: considering it a «relative noun» meaning الذي, and it is likewise in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of نعم.
The third: considering «ما» a qualified indefinite in the position of accusative as a tamyīz, the implied form being «نعم شيئا يعظكم به», with the fāʿil latent by necessity.
We have summarised the topic for you, and we may return to detail it again, so reflect.

safi-cedvel:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) is a vocative particle; (أيّ) is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative «[Note: (ها) is for alerting (tanbīh), with no position.]»; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (أيّ) or a badal (substitute) of it; (آمنوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أطيعوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) is a conjunction; (أطيعوا الرسول) is like أطيعوا الله; (الواو) is a conjunction; (أولي) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, since it is attached (mulḥaq) to the sound masculine plural; (الأمر) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (من) is a preposition and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أولي الأمر); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (تنازعتم) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive …, and (تم) is a pronoun, the fāʿil; (في شيء) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تنازعتم); (الفاء) links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (ردّوا) is like أطيعوا, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (إلى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ردّوه); (الواو) is a conjunction; (الرسول) is conjoined to the Name of Majesty, genitive like it; (إن كنتم) is like إن تنازعتم …, and (تم) is the noun of كان; (تؤمنون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تؤمنون); (اليوم) is conjoined to the Name of Majesty by the wāw, genitive like it; (الآخر) is a naʿt of اليوم, genitive; (ذا) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (خير) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أحسن) is conjoined to خير by the wāw, nominative like it; (تأويلا) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The vocative clause «يا أيها الذين» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أطيعوا الله» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أطيعوا الرسول» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «إن تنازعتم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «ردّوه …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كنتم تؤمنون» has no grammatical position, parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), in the context of urging.
The clause «تؤمنون …» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم … and the apodosis of the (second) condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: «فردوه إلى الله».
The clause «ذلك خير» has no grammatical position, a causal explanation (taʿlīl) of the first condition.

* Morphology:
(خير، أحسن): they may be two nouns of preference (ism tafḍīl), with the thing surpassed omitted, and they may be two pure adjectives without preference, i.e. «good» and «fine».
On the first meaning, خير and أحسن have the pattern أفعل, with the hamza dropped from the word خير because of frequent use; and خير and حسن (on the second meaning) have the patterns فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, and فعل with two fatḥas, respectively.

* Benefits:
1- Muslim narrated from the ḥadīth of Umm al-Ḥuṣayn: «Even if a slave is put in charge of you who leads you by the Book of Allah, hear and obey.» «فَإِنْ تَنازَعْتُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ»:
to the texts first; and if texts are not found, then to the general universal principles and the established aims of the Sharīʿa that cover all the main aspects of life. In that there is respect for the intellect and the granting to it of a place to work, and this is the task of practising scholars and of jurists exercising ijtihād.

safi-cedvel:114-114.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) the lā of generic negation; (خير) the noun of lā, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative; (في كثير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of lā; (من نجوى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of كثير, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلا) a particle of exception; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as the excepted in a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) «[Note: or a continuous one, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "the private talk of one who ordered…"]»; (أمر) a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and it is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (بصدقة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أمر); (أو) a conjunction; (معروف) maʿṭūf (conjoined) on صدقة, genitive (majrūr) like it; (أو) like the first; (إصلاح) conjoined on معروف, genitive like it; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to إصلاح; (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunctive; (من) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يفعل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (ابتغاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative «[Note: or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يفعل, i.e. "seeking the pleasure of Allah".]»; (مرضاة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (سوف) a particle of the future; (نؤتي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu", for majesty; (أجرا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (عظيما) naʿt of أجر, accusative.
The clause «لا خير في كثير ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أمر بصدقة» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «من يفعل ذلك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the resumptive clause.
The clause «يفعل ذلك ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: it is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of protasis and apodosis together.]».
The clause «سوف نؤتيه ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(نجوى): a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the quadriliteral ناجى, its pattern فعلى with fatḥa on the fāʾ; or it is an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb نجا ينجو الرجل زميله ("the man spoke privately with his companion"), of the bāb نصر.
Or it is the noun from it, and it may come with the meaning of "the one who converses privately" (المناجي).
(إصلاح): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb أصلح, its pattern إفعال, on the pattern of the past with kasra on the first letter, sukūn on the second, and an alif added before the last (al-Nisāʾ 35).

* Benefits:
- The merit of reconciling between people:
Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ṣafiyya bint Shayba from Umm Ḥabība, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «All the speech of the son of Adam is against him, not for him, except the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or enjoining what is right, or forbidding what is wrong.»
And from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: «He is not a liar who reconciles between people, conveying good or saying good.»
And from Abū al-Dardāʾ that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Shall I not tell you of what is better in rank than fasting, prayer and charity?» They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: «Reconciling between those at odds.»
And from Anas that the Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Ayyūb: «Shall I not direct you to a trade?» He said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: «Strive to reconcile between people when they fall out, and to bring them close when they grow distant.»

safi-cedvel:115-115.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (من يشاقق الرسول) like من يفعل ذلك «[Note: in the previous verse (114).]»; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشاقق); (ما) a maṣdar-forming (maṣdarī) particle; (تبيّن) a past verb; (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تبين) — or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الهدى —; (الهدى) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تبين له الهدى) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(الواو) conjunctive; (يتّبع) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), maʿṭūf (conjoined) on (يشاقق), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (غير) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (سبيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (المؤمنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (نولّ) an imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu", for majesty; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi; (تولى) a past verb, the fāʿil is "huwa", and it is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid), and the object of تولى is omitted, i.e. "what he turned to of misguidance"; (الواو) conjunctive; (نصل) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined on (نولّه), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and likewise نولّه; and (الهاء) a first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "naḥnu", for majesty; (جهنم) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) resumptive; (ساءت) a past verb, inflexible (jāmid), for expressing blame «[Note: or inflected (mutaṣarrif), and the fāʿil is optionally latent, its implied form being "hiya", and مصيرا is a tamyīz (specification) of the clause.]» ... and (التاء) for the feminine, and the fāʿil is an obligatorily latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya"; (مصيرا) a tamyīz of the latent pronoun, accusative «[Note: المصير is a mīmī maṣdar or a noun of place, and it may specify a masculine or a feminine pronoun ... The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is implied, i.e. جهنم.]».
The clause «من يشاقق ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause من يفعل ذلك in the previous verse.
The clause «يشاقق الرسول» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (من).
The clause «تبيّن له الهدى» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يتّبع ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined on the clause يشاقق.
The clause «نولّه ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تولّى» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «نصله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the apodosis clause نولّه.
The clause «ساءت» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(نولّه): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion due to the jussive; its pattern is نفعّه.
(نصله): it contains iʿlāl by deletion due to the jussive; its pattern is نفعه with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the ʿayn. It also contains deletion of the hamza for lightness, for its past is أصلى, and the analogical form of its imperfect would be نؤصلي; the deletion in it follows the course of يتقن.

safi-cedvel:116-116.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (لا) negating; (يغفر) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يشرك) an imperfect verb, passive, subjunctive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", referring to the associating (al-ishrāk) or to the deity worshipped «[Note: see verse (48) of this sura.]»; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشرك).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يشرك ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being يغفر, i.e. "He does not forgive associating [others] with Him".
(الواو) conjunctive; (يغفر) an imperfect verb like the first; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (دون) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) ... and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (اللام) a preposition and (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (يغفر); (يشاء) like يغفر. (الواو) resumptive; (من يشرك) like من يفعل «[Note: in verse (114) of this sura.]»; (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يشرك); (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) a particle of realization; (ضلّ) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (ضلالا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (بعيدا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يغفر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يغفر ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «يشرك به» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يغفر ما دون ذلك» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined on the clause لا يغفر ...
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «من يشرك ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يشرك بالله» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (من) «[Note: it is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of protasis and apodosis together.]».
The clause «ضلّ ضلالا ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:117-117.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) a particle of negation; (يدعون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يدعون), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (إناثا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunctive; (إن يدعون إلا شيطانا) like the preceding; (مريدا) a naʿt (adjective), accusative, of (شيطانا).
The first clause «يدعون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The second clause «يدعون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(يدعون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يدعوون; two quiescent letters met, so the wāw, the lām of the word, was deleted; its pattern is يفعون (al-Baqara 221).
(إناثا): plural of أنثى, a derived adjective, its pattern فعلى with ḍamma on the fāʾ; and the pattern of إناث is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(مريدا): a derived adjective from مرد يمرد, of the bāb نصر, its pattern فعيل.

safi-cedvel:163-163.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّا) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), and (نا) an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ (أوحينا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and (نا) a pronoun, the fāʿil (agent) (إلى) preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحينا), (الكاف) preposition [Note: or a noun meaning مثل (like), in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its qualifier.], (ما) maṣdar-forming particle (أوحينا) like the first.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أوحينا) is in the position of genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq.. i.e. «إيحاء كإيحائنا إلى نوح ...» (a revelation like Our revelation to Nūḥ ...).
(إلى نوح) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوحينا), (الواو) conjunction (النبيّين) conjoined to نوح, genitive (majrūr) like it, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of النبيّين [Note: it may not be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of النبيّين, because an adverb of time cannot validly be a ḥāl of a concrete (jāmid) noun], and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (أوحينا إلى إبراهيم) like أوحينا إلى نوح, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, since it is a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign (al-ʿalamiyya wa-l-ʿujma) (الواو) conjunction in the nine places (إسماعيل، إسحاق ... ، سليمان) nouns conjoined to the word إبراهيم by the conjunctions, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because they are all diptotes (الواو) conjunction (آتينا) like أوحينا (داود) first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (زبورا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «إنّا أوحينا ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أوحينا إليك»: in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أوحينا إلى نوح»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «أوحينا إلى إبراهيم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila of the particle-relative.
The clause «آتينا داود»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first clause أوحينا.

* Morphology:
«زبورا»: a concrete (jāmid) noun for the Book sent down to Dāwūd; its pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and it may take a ḍamma in one reading.

* Benefits:
The verse mentions a group of the names of the prophets, upon them be blessings and peace, such as إبراهيم - إسماعيل - إسحاق - يعقوب. If we survey the names of the prophets occurring in the Noble Quran, we find that all of them are barred from tanwīn (i.e. from ṣarf, full declension) for two reasons, namely being a proper name and being foreign, except صالحا - نوحا - شعيبا - محمدا - لوطا - هودا, the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all. What is meant by a foreign proper name is one transferred from the tongue of non-Arabs, in whatever language it may be. The noun is called "barred from tanwīn" or "barred from ṣarf" (diptote) because it cannot validly take tanwīn; so we say رأيت إبراهيم (I saw Ibrāhīm), and you may not say رأيت إبراهيما. It is well known that the diptote is put in the genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, as in our saying مررت بعثمان (I passed by ʿUthmān). But if the diptote is a muḍāf or made definite with al-, it takes the genitive with the kasra, as in our saying مررت بمساجد المدينة (I passed by the mosques of the city) or مررت بالمساجد العامرة بالمصلين (I passed by the mosques full of worshippers); مساجد is a diptote because it is one of the forms of the ultimate plural (ṣiyagh muntahā al-jumūʿ), on the pattern مفاعل. So the diptote is not always put in the genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra; take note of that.

safi-cedvel:164-165.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction (رسلا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being أرسلنا (We sent) or أمرنا (We commanded) [Note: the implied form of the omitted governor may be (قصصنا) (We related); in that case the clause (قد قصصنا) becomes explicative, with no grammatical position.], (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq) (قصصنا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi [Note: that is by giving قصصاناهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is قصصناهم] the implied sense of سمّيناهم (We named them).], (على) preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قصصنا), (من) preposition (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (قصصنا), (الواو) conjunction (رسلا) like the first (لم) particle of negation and jussive (نقصص) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and (هم) mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu" (We), for majesty (عليك) like the first, attached to (نقصص), (الواو) resumptive (كلّم) past verb (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) (موسى) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif (تكليما) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «(أرسلنا) رسلا ...»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first clause أوحينا [Note: in the previous verse (163).].
The clause «قد قصصناهم ...»: in the position of accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of (رسلا).
The clause «(أرسلنا) رسلا (the second)»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first clause.
The clause «لم نقصصهم ...»: in the position of accusative, a naʿt of (رسلا).
The clause «كلّم الله موسى ...»: has no grammatical position, a parenthetical resumption (istiʾnāf iʿtirāḍī).
(165) (رسلا) badal (substitute) of the first (رسلا), accusative like it [Note: it may be a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being أرسلنا; it may also be a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa) — it being a concrete (jāmid) word that is qualified.], (مبشّرين) naʿt of (رسلا), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (الواو) conjunction (منذرين) conjoined to مبشّرين, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (اللام) the lām of causation (taʿlīl) (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle (لا) negating (يكون) imperfect verb, accusative by أن, defective (nāqiṣ) (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) [Note: it may be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of حجّة, and then the khabar becomes the preposition and genitive noun على الله.], (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of حجّة — a naʿt that has come before the qualified noun — (حجّة) noun of يكون, nominative (بعد) adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative, attached to (حجّة) or to a naʿt of it (الرسل) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and it is on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «بعد إرسال الرسل» (after the sending of the messengers).
The interpreted maṣdar (ألا يكون ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to the implied verb (أرسلنا).
(الواو) resumptive (كان) defective past verb (الله) the Divine Name, noun of كان, nominative (عزيزا) khabar of كان, accusative (حكيما) second khabar, accusative.
The clause «يكون.. حجّة»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative «أن».
The clause «كان الله عزيزا ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(تكليما): the regular maṣdar (verbal noun) of the quadriliteral verb كلّم; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Benefits:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿رُسُلًا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ — the word رسلا in the noble verse has occupied the grammarians and the parsers, and they have taken different positions in its i'rab, namely:
1- We parse it as a badal (substitute) of the رسلا that preceded it in the previous verse, namely His saying ﴿وَرُسُلًا قَدْ قَصَصْناهُمْ عَلَيْكَ﴾.
2- A mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being أرسلنا رسلا (We sent messengers).
3- That it be parsed as a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa) for what follows it, as you say مررت بزيد رجلا صالحا (I passed by Zayd, a righteous man).
4- That it be parsed as a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb of praise, its implied form being أعني (I mean). Through these accounts we cannot refute any view or declare it wrong, and these accounts do not conflict with the meaning.
But we prefer the first view: it is the closest to correctness and the one that comes first to mind, and it requires no implied element. The remaining accounts require implication and interpretation. The rule in the science of the foundations of grammar (uṣūl al-naḥw) requires that when two analyses are equal, one requiring an implied element and the other not, then the absence of implication is preferable.

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(حرّمت) a passive past verb ... and the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (حرّمت), (أمهات) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunctive in the seven [Translator's note: the source reads «لسبعة», evidently for «السبعة», "the seven".] places; (بناتكم....، أمهاتكم) nouns annexed to the pronouns or to overt nouns, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (أمهات) by the conjunctions, nominative like it; (اللاتي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (أمّهات); (أرضعن) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (النون) the fāʿil (agent), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) conjunctive; (أخوات) maʿṭūf to (أمهات), nominative like it, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من الرضاعة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أخوات); (الواو) conjunctive; (أمهات) maʿṭūf to the first (أمّهات), nominative like it; (نساء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (ربائب) maʿṭūf to (أمّهات), nominative like it, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (اللاتي) like the first, a naʿt of (ربائب); (في حجور) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من نساء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of (اللاتي); (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (اللاتي) like the first, a naʿt of (نسائكم); (دخلتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. (وتم) the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition and (هنّ) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (دخلتم). (الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (لم) negative only; (تكونوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) [Note: and the jussive-governor, according to the view of the majority of exegetes, is (لم), because it is the stronger.], the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun of (تكون); (دخلتم) like the first, and likewise (بهنّ), (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لا) the lā of generic negation; (جناح) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative (manṣūb); (عليكم) like the first, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of lā. (الواو) conjunctive; (حلائل) maʿṭūf to the first (أمّهات), nominative like it; (أبناء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of (أبنائكم); (من أصلاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila of the relative, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (تجمعوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (تجمعوا) [Translator's note: the source repeats a segment here by mistake, giving (بين) the description belonging to (تجمعوا) before restating it correctly; reproduced as written.], (الأختين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
(إلّا ما قد سلف) its i'rab was given in the preceding verse.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تجمعوا ...) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the first (أمهاتكم).
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (كان) a defective past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (غفورا) the khabar of kāna, accusative; (رحيما) a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أرضعنكم لا» محلّ لها [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is misplaced in the source; reproduced as written.] has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the first relative (اللاتي).
The clause «دخلتم بهنّ» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (اللاتي).
The clause «تكونوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive, having the force of a parenthesis.
The clause «دخلتم بهنّ (the second)» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of (تكونوا).
The clause «لا جناح عليكم» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تجمعوا..» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «قد سلف» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله كان..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كان غفورا..» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(بناتكم): plural of بنت; the tāʾ in it is a substitute for its omitted lām, which is either a wāw — which is the predominant view — or a yāʾ. The pattern of بنت is فعت and the pattern of the plural is فعات with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(أخوات): plural of أخت; the tāʾ in it is a substitute for the omitted wāw, because it is from الإخوة.
(خالات): plural of خالة; the alif in it is converted from a wāw, because they said أخوال.
(ربائبكم): plural of ربيبة, the feminine of ربيب, فعيل in the sense of مفعول, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the quadriliteral ربّى يربّي ... and the hamza is converted from a yāʾ because it comes after an augmentative alif.
(حجور): plural of حجر, a noun for the front of the garment; it was used as a metonymy for presence originally [Translator's note: so in the source: «وكنّى به عن الوجود أصلا».].
(حلائل): plural of حليلة, originally a ṣifa mushabbaha from the triliteral حلّ يحلّ, of the bāb of ضرب, meaning the wife; then it became a noun. Its pattern is فعيلة.
(أصلاب): plural of صلب, a noun meaning the back; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn ... (and see verse 7 of Sūrat al-Ṭāriq).

* Rhetoric:
1- Metonymy (kināya): in His saying, Exalted is He: «دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ»; it is a metonymy for intercourse, like their saying "he built upon her" and "he drew the veil over her", and touching has the same ruling.

* Benefits:
1- أخ and أخت, ابن and بنت.
Their [the two words'] origin is أخو and بنو; the wāw was dropped and the tāʾ was added to them to distinguish between masculine and feminine.
Part Five
The remainder of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
from verse 24 to verse 147

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (المحصنات) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first (أمهاتكم) in the preceding verse; (من النساء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (المحصنات); (إلّا) a particle of exception; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) by exception [Note: connected or disconnected, according to the interpretation; both are valid.], (ملكت) a past verb ... and (التاء) is for the feminine; (أيمان) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (كتاب) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "He prescribed", i.e. made obligatory [Note: or mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "apply the Book of Allah".], (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the omitted verb. (الواو) resumptive; (أحل) a passive past verb; (لكم) like (عليكم), attached to (أحل), (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (وراء) an adverb, accusative, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and (اللام) is for distance and (كم) for addressing the plural; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (تبتغوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil; (بأموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb (تبتغوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (محصنين) ḥāl, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (غير) a second ḥāl, accusative; (مسافحين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبتغوا ...) is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) of (ما).. or in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition [Note: the implied form being: "it has been made lawful for you.. by your seeking" or "so that you seek" ... and the preposition phrase is attached to (أحل)].
