(الفاء) resumptive; (ما) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: it may be a relative, as mubtadaʾ, the khabar being (آتوهن) with the fāʾ added, and the linking pronoun omitted, i.e. "for its sake", and the preposition phrase (منهنّ) attached to a ḥāl of the relative.], (استمتعتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and (تم) an agent pronoun; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (استمتعتم), and the pronoun refers back to the wording of (ما); (من) a preposition and (هنّ) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (استمتعتم) [Note: (من) is partitive or explanatory, according to the i'rab of (ما).], (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (آتوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (أجور) the second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هنّ) muḍāf ilayhi; (فريضة) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl of (أجورهن), accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb ... or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being either its description or its synonym.], (الواو) resumptive; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (جناح) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative; (عليكم) like the first, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of lā; (في) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to the omitted khabar; (تراضيتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ...
and (تم) the fāʿil; (به) like the first, attached to (تراضيتم), (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun in (به), (الفريضة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna; (كان) a defective past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (عليما) the khabar of kāna, accusative; (حكيما) a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «ملكت أيمانكم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative.
The clause «... كتاب الله» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أحل لكم ما وراء ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تبتغوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ما استمتعتم به» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «استمتعتم به» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «آتوهن ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا جناح عليكم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تراضيتم به ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله كان ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كان عليما ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(المحصنات): plural of المحصنة, the feminine of المحصن, a passive participle from the quadriliteral أحصن; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(كتاب): the maṣdar of كتب يكتب, of the bāb of نصر, in the sense of "to make obligatory"; its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ; and the verb has other maṣdars: كتب with fatḥa then sukūn, كتبة with kasra on the kāf, and كتابة with kasra on the kāf.
(محصنين): plural of محصن, an active participle from the quadriliteral أحصن; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(مسافحين): plural of مسافح, an active participle from the quadriliteral سافح; its pattern is مفاعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, Exalted is He: غَيْرَ مُسافِحِينَ — fornication is likened to pouring water into rivers, because the fornicator has no aim except pouring out the sperm only, not offspring.
2- Explicit metaphor: in His saying, Exalted is He: فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ — He borrowed the word "wages" (الأجور) for the dowry.

* Benefits:
The operation of «لا» of generic negation.
a- Its noun is made indeclinable on that by which it would be made accusative: if it is a single word it is indeclinable on the fatḥa, and it is indeclinable on the yāʾ if it is a dual or a sound masculine plural.
b- If it is annexed (muḍāf) or resembling the annexed, it is declinable, accusative — by the yāʾ if it is a dual or a sound masculine plural.

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); (لم) a particle of negation; (يستطع) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of (يستطع); (طولا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) [Note: the object may be the interpreted maṣdar — as will come — and (طولا) a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: "whoever of you is unable to marry because of lack of means" ... and it may be accusative as a maṣdar, standing in for it because it is its synonym [Translator's note: the source prints «مردافه», evidently for «مرادفه», "its synonym".], i.e.: "whoever is unable to marry ..." — so al-ṭawl means ability.], (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (ينكح) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (المحصنات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (المؤمنات) naʿt (adjective), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ينكح) is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of (طولا) [Note: or it is the mafʿūl bihi of the verb ... and the two cases given in the previous footnote are valid for (طولا). The interpreted maṣdar may be genitive by a preposition, namely إلى or the lām, attached to (يستطع) or to an omitted naʿt of (طولا).. just as it may be the mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar (طولا), if the latter is the object of the verb.].
(الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (من) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "marry" [Note: (ما) here means the kind that the right hands possess.], (ملكت) a past verb ... and (التاء) is for the feminine; (أيمان) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من فتيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the object pronoun referring back to (ما), and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (المؤمنات) a naʿt of (فتيات), genitive like it; (الواو) parenthetical; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أعلم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (بإيمان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعلم), and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (بعض) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (من بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (الفاء) conjunctive; (انكحوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (بإذن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (انكحوا); (أهل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هنّ) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (آتوهنّ) like (انكحوهنّ); (أجور) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هنّ) muḍāf ilayhi; (بالمعروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl of the agent of (آتوهن) [Note: it may be attached to (آتوهن), or to (انكحوهن بإذن أهلهن).] (محصنات) ḥāl, accusative, of the object pronoun in (انكحوهن), the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (غير) a second ḥāl, accusative; (مسافحات) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunctive; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; (متخذات) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (غير), accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (أخدان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
(الفاء) resumptive; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to the content of the apodosis; (أحصن) a passive past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (النون) a pronoun, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of (إذا); (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (أتين) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis ...
and (النون) the fāʿil; (بفاحشة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أتين) by its being made to include the meaning of (قمن) [Translator's note: so in the source: «بتضمينه معنى قمن», i.e. "they committed".]; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of (إن); (على) a preposition and (هنّ) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (نصف) a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (على المحصنات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of (ما); (من العذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the agent pronoun in the ṣila, which refers back to (ما). (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (اللام) a preposition; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذا); (خشي) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (العنت) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (منكم) like the first, attached to a ḥāl of the agent of (خشي); (الواو) resumptive; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (تصبروا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تصبروا ...) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
(خير) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is the interpreted maṣdar, nominative; (لكم) like (منكم), attached to (خير). (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (غفور) khabar, nominative; (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «من لم يستطع ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لم يستطع ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «ينكح ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The implied clause «انكحوا» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ملكت أيمانكم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «الله أعلم ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical.
The clause «بعضكم من بعض» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun of address in (أيمانكم) [Note: because the muḍāf (أيمان) is part of the muḍāf ilayhi, which is the pronoun of the addressee.].
The clause «انكحوهنّ» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the implied clause (انكحوا).
The clause «آتوهنّ ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause (انكحوهنّ).
The clause «أحصّ ...» [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for «أحصنّ».] is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of (إذا) to it.
The clause «أتين..» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of the non-jussive condition (إذا).
The clause «عليهن نصف ما ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition (إن), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ذلك لمن خشي ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «خشي العنت ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative.
The nominal clause made of the interpreted maṣdar and its khabar has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تصبروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «الله غفور ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(طولا): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb طال يطول, and its meaning is ability. (فتيات): plural of فتاة, and the alif is converted from a yāʾ because it returned in the plural; the masculine plural is فتية and فتيان; it [the yāʾ] came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to an alif.
(أعلم): a derived adjective that is not for the comparative (tafḍīl), even though it comes on the pattern أفعل; it means عالم or عليم (al-Baqara — 40).
(أخدان): plural of خدن, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the quadriliteral verb خادن, irregularly; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn ... and the pattern of أخدان is أفعال.
(متّخذات): plural of متخذة, the feminine of متخذ, an active participle from the five-letter اتخذ; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(العنت): an aurally transmitted maṣdar of the verb عنت يعنت, of the bāb of فرح; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Benefits:
1- There is disagreement among the scholars about «من» in His saying, Exalted is He: فَمِنْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ.
a- One group holds that «من» is redundant, and the implied form is «then let him marry what [your right hands] possess».
b- Another group holds that it is not redundant, but rather the verb and its object have been omitted, and the implied form is «then let him marry a woman from among what your right hands possess».
On the second view we attach «the preposition phrase» to the adjective of "woman", which is omitted together with its adjective, and its implied form is «being».
2- The free and the slaves are of one another.
It is worth pausing before the Quran's expression of the reality of the human relations that exist between the free and the enslaved in Islam, and of this religion's view of this matter when it established Islamic society. It does not call slave-girls "female slaves" (رقيقات) or "bondwomen" (إماء); it calls them only «young women» (فتيات): «فَمِنْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ مِنْ فَتَياتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِناتِ». And it does not distinguish between the free and the unfree with a racial distinction touching human origin — as were the beliefs and considerations prevailing across the whole earth in those days, and as they still are now in some societies such as South Africa and the United States — rather, it reminds us of the single origin, and makes the human bond and the bond of faith the axis of connection: «وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمانِكُمْ بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ».
Likewise, it does not call their owners "masters" but calls them "family" (أهل): «فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ».

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(للرجال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (نصيب) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (من) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun «[Note: Or an indefinite noun that is qualified (nakira mawṣūfa) ... and the clause after it is its naʿt (adjective), in the position of a genitive.]», in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt of نصيب; (ترك) a past verb; (الوالدان) fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the alif; (الواو) a conjunction; (الأقربون) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (الوالدان), nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (الواو) a conjunction; (للنساء نصيب ...
والأقربون) like للرجال ... والأقربون; (ممّا) like the first, attached to what the first is attached to, because it is a badal (substitute) from it with the preposition repeated «[Note: This badal is a substitute from His saying: للنساء نصيب ممّا ترك ...]»; (قلّ) a past verb, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa", and it is the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid); (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (قلّ); (أو) a conjunction; (كثر) like قلّ; (نصيبا) an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the [notion of] settled existence (al-istiqrār) in His saying للرجال نصيب «[Note: Different views have been reported on the i'rab of this word.. It is said to be a ḥāl from the agent of قلّ or كثر; it is said to be mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied verb, i.e. He made obligatory for them a share, or Allah made it a share; it is said to be accusative as an emphatic maṣdar, as you say: له عليّ كذا وكذا حقّا واجبا (he is owed such-and-such by me, as a binding right); and it is said to be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. نصيبه نصيبا ...]»; (مفروضا) naʿt of (نصيبا), accusative (manṣūb) like it.
The clause «للرجال نصيب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ترك الوالدان» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «للنساء نصيب» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ترك الوالدان (the second)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «قلّ ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative noun (ما).
The clause «كثر» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قلّ.

* Morphology:
(مفروضا) passive participle from the triliteral فرض, of the pattern (bāb) ضرب; its wazn is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (إذا) an adverb of future time including the meaning of a condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis; (حضر) a past verb; (القسمة) a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (أولوا) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw, for it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; (القربى) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddara) on the alif; (الواو) a conjunction; (اليتامى) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the agent, nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif; (المساكين) conjoined to the agent by the conjunction, nominative like it; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (ارزقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent, and (هم) a pronoun, direct object; (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (ارزقوا); the pronoun comes masculine because it refers to what is divided, understood from His saying (القسمة); (الواو) a conjunction; (قولوا ... معروفا) its i'rab has passed «[Note: in verse (5) of this surah.]».
The clause «حضر ...» أولوا ... is in the position of a genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ارزقوهم» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قولوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.

* Morphology:
(القسمة) a noun from الاقتسام (dividing); its wazn is فعلة with kasra then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of command; (يخش) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); (لو) a non-jussive conditional; (تركوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the agent; (من خلف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تركوا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ذرّيّة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (ضعافا) naʿt (adjective), accusative; (خافوا) like تركوا; (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (خافوا); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (يتّقوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent; (الله) the Name of Majesty, direct object, governed by ليتّقوا ... As for the object of ليخش, it is omitted, explained by the mentioned Name of Majesty; (الواو) a conjunction; (ليقولوا) like ليتّقوا; (قولا) a direct object, accusative; (سديدا) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «ليخش الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لو تركوا..» خافوا has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «خافوا عليهم» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ليتقوا الله» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if fear of Allah enters their hearts, then let them fear Allah.
The clause «ليقولوا ...» is conjoined to the clause ليتّقوا الله.

* Morphology:
(يخش) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion suited to the jussive; its wazn is يفع.
(سديدا) an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) from سدّ يسدّ, of the patterns (bāb) ضرب and فتح, i.e. to be upright in word and deed; it carries the meaning of the active and of the passive, and its wazn is فعيل.

* Benefits:
1- The conditional لو: we alluded earlier to some of the rulings of this «لو», and to complete the benefit we see fit to cover some of its rulings that we have not dealt with before. The grammarians have made fine efforts concerning the rulings of this particle. It is well known among the grammarians as a particle of impossibility for impossibility (ḥarf imtināʿ li-mtināʿ); then they went on to detail that, saying that it is divided into two kinds:
The first is that it is specific to future time, and so is equivalent to the conditional «إن», as in the saying of Abū Ṣakhr al-Hudhalī:
ولو تلتقي أصداؤنا بعد موتنا ... ومن دون رمسينا من الأرض سبب
(Should our echoes meet after our death, with a stretch of earth between our two graves,)
لظل صدى صوتي وإن كنت رمّة ... لصوت صدى ليلى يهشّ ويطرب
(the echo of my voice, though I be decayed bones, would keep rejoicing and thrilling at the voice of Laylā's echo.)
If a past verb follows it, we interpret it as future, as in the saying of the Exalted: «وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعافاً خافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ».
The second is that it relates to the past, and this is the most frequent of its uses; it entails the impossibility of its condition because of the impossibility of its apodosis «[Translator's note: so in the source; the usual formulation is the impossibility of the apodosis because of the impossibility of the condition.]». The grammarians have laid down a rule for its condition and apodosis that is not without charm, nor without benefit:
If it enters upon two affirmative verbs, they are negative [in meaning], as in «لو جاءني لأكرمته» (had he come to me, I would have honoured him), meaning that he did not come to me and I did not honour him. Conversely, if it enters upon two negated verbs, they are «affirmative», as in لو لم يجدّ في العلم لما نال منه شيئا (had he not striven in learning, he would not have gained anything of it), the meaning being that he strove and gained learning. More charming still, if it enters upon a negation and an affirmation, the negation becomes affirmation and the affirmation negation, as in: «لو لم يهتم بأمر دنياه لعاش عالة على الناس» (had he not attended to his worldly affairs, he would have lived as a burden on people), the meaning being that he attended to his worldly affairs and did not live as a burden on people.
The conditional لو is absolutely specific to the verb; occasionally a noun may follow it, governed by a necessarily omitted verb explained by what comes after it, as in the poet's saying:
اخلّاي لو غير الحمام أصابكم ... عتبت ولكن ما على الدهر معتب
(My friends, had something other than death struck you, I would have reproached [it]; but there is no reproaching fate.)
The study has a continuation regarding its specificity and its apodosis. We content ourselves with what we have said, and leave the rest to whoever is inquisitive in the science of grammar; let him refer to it in its places in the extended works.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, the noun of inna; (يأكلون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أموال) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (اليتامى) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddara) on the alif; (ظلما) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. wrongfully «[Note: It may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).]»; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (يأكلون) like the first; (في بطون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl from (نارا) — a naʿt (adjective) placed before the noun it qualifies — and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (نارا) a direct object, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (السين) a particle of futurity; (يصلون) like يأكلون; (سعيرا) a direct object, accusative.
The clause «إنّ الذين يأكلون..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يأكلون..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّما يأكلون ...» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «سيصلون سعيرا» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause إنّما يأكلون.

* Morphology:
(سيصلون) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion: the alif — the final radical (lām) of the word — was deleted because it came quiescent before the quiescent wāw of the plural, and the letter before the wāw was given fatḥa to indicate the deleted alif. Its wazn is سيفعون with fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(سعيرا) a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the flame of fire, from سعر يسعر النار, of the pattern (bāb) فتح, i.e. he kindled it; its wazn is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- The mention of «البطون» (bellies) is for emphasis and exaggeration, as in the saying of the Exalted: «يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ», though speaking is only with the mouth; and His saying, Glorified be He: «وَلا طائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَناحَيْهِ», though a bird only flies with wings.
2- Mursal (non-metaphorical) trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in His saying «نارا».
«النار» is a majāz mursal by mentioning the effect and meaning the cause. They also allowed metaphor (istiʿāra) here, by likening the orphans' wealth that was consumed to fire, because it obliterates whatever is with it.
3- «وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيراً»: the basic meaning of الصلي is nearness to fire, and here it is used figuratively for entering.

* Benefits:
1- «إِنَّما يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ ناراً»: we had a pause on the restraining «إنما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and now we return to the «ما» attached to «إنّ» and its sisters, especially regarding how it is written. This «ما» is of three kinds: the redundant ما, which restrains from governing; the relative ما; and the maṣdar-forming ما, which is interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar. The restraining one is written joined to the particle preceding it, as in «إنما, كأنما and لعلّما». The relative and the maṣdar-forming are written separate from what precedes them, as in the saying of the Exalted: «ما عِنْدَكُمْ يَنْفَدُ», and as in إن ما تستقيم حسن (your being upright is good): the first is relative and the second maṣdar-forming. One of discernment will perceive the differences between them.

safi-cedvel:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(السين) a particle of the future; (تجدون) an imperfect verb, nominative ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (آخرين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (يريدون) like تجدون; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يأمنوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (يأمنوا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to يأمنوكم, subjunctive like it; (قوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأمنوكم) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being يريدون.
(كلّما) an adverb meaning "when" containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis أركسوا; (ردّوا) a passive past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma ... and the wāw is a pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلى الفتنة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ردّوا); (أركسوا) like ردّوا; (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أركسوا). (الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (لم) a particle of negation; (يعتزلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) [Note: The verb is made jussive by the jussive particle (لم) according to the view of the majority, but the verb comes to indicate the past, contrary to the meaning of the condition.] , the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (يلقوا) like يعتزلوا and conjoined to it, the preceding negation governing it; (إلى) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يلقوا); (السلم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (يكفوا أيديهم) like يلقوا السلم ... and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (خذوهم ... ثقفتموهم) the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given [Note: in verse (89) of this surah.] , (الواو) conjunction; (أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (الكاف) a particle of address; (جعلنا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (لكم) like إليكم, attached to an omitted second object of the verb جعلنا; (عليهم) like إليكم, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (سلطانا), which is mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (مبينا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «ستجدون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يريدون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «يأمنوكم» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن):
The clause «يأمنوا قومهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يأمنوكم.
The clause «ردّوا» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أركسوا ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لم يعتزلوكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يلقوا إليكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعتزلوكم.
The clause «يكفوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعتزلوكم.
The clause «خذوهم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «اقتلوهم» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause خذوهم.
The clause «ثقفتموهم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أولئك جعلنا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعتزلوكم.
The clause «جعلنا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).

safi-cedvel:92-92.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; (لمؤمن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of كان; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يقتل) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb); its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (مؤمنا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (خطأ) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its description, accusative [Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) on the interpretation of a derived word, i.e. مخطئا ("erring").] .
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقتل) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of كان.
(الواو) conjunction; (من) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (قتل) a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (مؤمنا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (خطأ) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, accusative [Note: Or a ḥāl on the interpretation of a derived word, i.e. مخطئا.] , (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (تحرير) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "العقاب" ("the penalty") or "المسؤولية" ("the responsibility") or "الواجب" ("the obligation") [Note: It may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted before it, the implied form being: عليه تحرير رقبة ("upon him is the freeing of a slave").] , (رقبة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (مؤمنة) naʿt (adjective) of رقبة, genitive like it; (الواو) conjunction; (دية) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to تحرير, nominative like it; (مسلّمة) naʿt of دية, nominative like it; (إلى أهله) a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi, attached to (مسلّمة); (إلا) a particle of exception; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يصدّقوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يصدقوا) is in the position of accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because the blood-money is not of the kind of giving in charity [Note: Some allowed the exception to be connected, it being the exception of the blood-money in the case of giving it in charity from the generality of circumstances.] .
(الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كان) an incomplete past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, its noun a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (من قوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of كان; (عدوّ) naʿt of قوم, genitive like it; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of عدو [Note: Or attached to عدو, taking it as a maṣdar (verbal noun).] , (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (مؤمن) khabar, nominative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (تحرير رقبة مؤمنة) like the first. (الواو) conjunction; (إن كان من قوم) like the first; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (بينهم) like بينكم and conjoined to it; (ميثاق) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (دية) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "العقاب" or "المسؤولية" or "الواجب" [Note: It may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted and placed before it, the implied form being: عليه دية ("upon him is blood-money").] , (مسلّمة إلى أهله.. رقبة) like the preceding; (الفاء) conjunction; (من) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (لم) only a particle of negation; (يجد) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis [Note: The verb is made jussive by the jussive particle (لم) according to the view of the majority, but the verb comes to indicate the past, contrary to the meaning of the condition.] , its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (صيام) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "الواجب" [Note: Or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted and fronted, the implied form being: عليه صيام ("upon him is fasting").] , (شهرين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (متتابعين) naʿt, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (توبة) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, the implied form being تاب عليكم توبة ("He turned to you in repentance").] , i.e. that was legislated as a repentance from Allah; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of توبة; (الواو) resumptive; (كان) an incomplete past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of كان, nominative; (عليما) the khabar of كان, accusative; (حكيما) a second khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «ما كان لمؤمن ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يقتل ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «من قتل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قتل مؤمنا» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «1» .
The clause «(الواجب) تحرير ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «يصّدّقوا» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «كان من قوم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to من قتل ...
The clause «هو مؤمن» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «(الواجب) تحرير ... (the second)» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «كان من قوم (the second)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من قتل ...
The clause «(العقاب) دية ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «من لم يجد» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the second clause كان.
The clause «لم يجد ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «2» .
The clause «(الواجب) صيام» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «... توبة من الله» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كان الله عليما ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(خطأ): the maṣdar of خطئ يخطأ, of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(تحرير): a regular maṣdar of the four-letter verb حرر; its pattern is تفعيل, with the addition of a tāʾ to its past form, the lightening (un-doubling) of the ʿayn of the verb, and the addition of a yāʾ before the final letter.
(دية): a maṣdar used as a noun, from the verb ودي يدي, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is علة, so it contains iʿlāl (phonological change) by deletion of the fāʾ of the word; its origin is (ودية), with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مسلّمة): a passive participle from the four-letter سلّم, feminine of مسلم; its pattern is مفعّلة, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(يصدّقوا): it contains the substitution of the tāʾ of iftiʿāl with a ṣād and its assimilation into the fāʾ of the word; its pattern is يتفعّلوا.

safi-cedvel:60-63.t:
* I'rab:
(ألم تر إلى الذين) «[Note: See verse (44) of this sūra, where it was parsed.]»; (يزعمون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) …, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), for emphasis, and (هم) is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of أن; (أمنوا) is a past verb and its fāʿil; (الباء) is a preposition; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (آمنوا); (أنزل) is a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو», and it is the resumptive pronoun (ʿāʾid); (إلى) is a preposition and (الكاف) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل); (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما أنزل) is like the first and conjoined to it; (من قبل) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the second (أنزل), and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنهم آمنوا) stands in place of the two objects of يزعمون.
(يريدون) is like يزعمون; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle; (يتحاكموا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلى الطاغوت) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتحاكموا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتحاكموا) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by يريدون.
(الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (أمروا) is a past verb, passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; (أن يكفروا) is like أن يتحاكموا; (الباء) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يكفروا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكفروا) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, governed by (أمروا) «[Note: It may be genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, i.e. «بأن يكفروا», attached to (أمروا).]».
(الواو) is a conjunction; (يريد) is an imperfect verb, nominative; (الشيطان) is the fāʿil, nominative; (أن) is like the first; (يضلّ) is an imperfect verb, accusative, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (ضلالا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar «[Note: ضلال is the maṣdar of the triliteral ضلّ; as for the maṣdar of أضلّ يضل, it is إضلال; therefore the maṣdar of the triliteral stood in for it, because it coincides with it in derivation.]», accusative; (بعيدا) is a naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضلّهم) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, governed by يريد.
The clause «تر إلى الذين …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يزعمون …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «آمنوا» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The clause «أنزل إليك» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first relative (ما).
The clause «أنزل من قبلك» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «يريدون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يزعمون.
The clause «يتحاكموا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «قد أمروا …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يريدون.
The clause «يكفروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «يريد الشيطان …» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يريدون.
The clause «يضلّهم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third particle relative (أن).
(61) (الواو) is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time carrying the meaning of the condition, attached to (رأيت); (قيل) is a past verb, passive; (اللام) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (قيل); (تعالوا) is a non-inflecting (jāmid) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn because it is joined to the wāw of the plural …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلى ما) is like بما, attached to (تعالوا); (أنزل) is a past verb; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (الرسول) is genitive by إلى, attached to (تعالوا), so it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first genitive noun; (رأيت) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn …, and (التاء) is the fāʿil; (المنافقين) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (يصدّون) is an imperfect verb, nominative …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (عنك) is like إليك, attached to (يصدّون); (صدودا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The clause «قيل لهم» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تعالوا» is in the position of nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil «[Note: But according to المجهور «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «الجمهور» (the majority)]» the nāʾib fāʿil is implied, i.e. «قيل لهم القول», and the clause is explicative. We have preferred the i'rab above because the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl) for the active verb. (See verse 11 of Sūrat al-Baqara.)]».
The clause «أنزل الله» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «رأيت المنافقين» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يصدون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of المنافقين.
(62) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (كيف إذا) «[Note: See its i'rab in verse (41) of this sūra.]»; (أصابت) is a past verb …, and (التاء) is for the feminine, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (مصيبة) is the fāʿil, nominative; (بما) is like the first, attached to (أصابتهم) «[Note: (ما) may be a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive, attached to (أصابتهم), i.e.: «أصابتهم مصيبة بفعل أيديهم».]»; (قدمت) is like أصابت; (أيدي) is the fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ثم) is a conjunction; (جاؤوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (يحلفون) is an imperfect verb, nominative …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb (يحلفون); (إن) is a particle of negation; (أردنا) is a past verb and its fāʿil; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (إحسانا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (توفيقا) is conjoined to (إحسانا), accusative like it. The clause «كيف (الأمر) …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to a preceding resumptive clause.
The clause «أصابتهم مصيبة» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قدّمت أيديهم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «جاؤوك» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause أصابتهم.
The clause «يحلفون …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of جاؤوك.
The clause «أردنا» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.
(63) (أولئك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) …, and (الكاف) is for address; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as the khabar; (يعلم) is an imperfect verb, nominative; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; (في قلوب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila of ما, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) is a conjunction linking the effect to the cause «[Note: Or it links the apodosis of an implied condition.]». (أعرض) is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (عنهم) is like عنك, attached to (أعرض); (الواو) is a conjunction; (عظ) is like أعرض, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (قل لهم) is like أعرض عنهم, and the preposition is attached to (قل); (في أنفس) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قل) on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: «في حقّ أنفسهم» «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of قل, i.e. while you are alone with them, confiding the counsel to them in private.]», and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (قولا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (بليغا) is a naʿt, accusative.
The clause «أولئك الذين» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يعلم الله …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أعرض عنهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أولئك الذين «[Note: Or it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: «إن كان ذلك حالهم فأعرض عنهم».]».
The clause «عظهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أعرض عنهم.
The clause «قل لهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أعرض عنهم.

* Morphology:
(صدودا): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb صدّ يصدّ, of the bāb of نصر and the bāb of ضرب; its pattern is فعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and it is intransitive; the one from the bāb of نصر is transitive, its maṣdar being صدّ with fatḥa then sukūn.
(توفيقا): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral وفّق; its pattern is تفعيل, by adding the tāʾ at the beginning of the past, dropping the doubling and adding a yāʾ before its last letter.
(بليغا): a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the verb بلغ يبلغ, of the bāb of كرم; its pattern is فعيل.

* Benefits:
From the etiquette of social life:
His saying, the Exalted: وَقُلْ لَهُمْ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلًا بَلِيغاً — in this verse there is a moral and social etiquette, namely following the method of privacy and being alone with someone in giving counsel, for it is more effective in impact and more beneficial for the one counselled.

safi-cedvel:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is negating; (أرسلنا) is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (رسول) is genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (اللام) is for causation (taʿlīl); (يطاع) is an imperfect verb, passive, accusative by a concealed «أن», and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يطاع) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أرسلنا).
(بإذن) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (يطاع) «[Note: It may be attached to the verb يطاع, with the bāʾ being causal, i.e. «يطاع بأمر الله».]»; (الله) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لو) is a non-jussive conditional; (أنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of أنّ; (إذ) is an adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (جاؤوك); (ظلموا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أنفس) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (جاؤوا) is like ظلموا, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم … جاؤوك) is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being «ثبت», i.e.: «لو ثبت مجيئهم حين ظلموا أنفسهم …».
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (استغفروا) is like ظلموا; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (استغفر) is a past verb; (اللام) is a preposition and (هم) is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (استغفر); (الرسول) is the fāʿil, nominative; (اللام) occurs in the apodosis of لو; (وجدوا) is like ظلموا; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (توابا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (رحيما) is a ḥāl of the pronoun in (توّابا), accusative «[Note: It may be a naʿt (adjective) of (توابا), or a badal (substitute) of it.]».
The clause «ما أرسلنا …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يطاع …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «(ثبت) مجيئهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ظلموا …» is in the position of genitive by (إذ) being annexed to it.
The clause «جاؤوك» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The clause «استغفروا الله» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause جاؤوك.
The clause «استغفر لهم الرسول» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause جاؤوك.
The clause «وجدوا …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of address): in His saying, the Exalted: وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمُ الرَّسُولُ.
For He shifted from the second person to the third person, to magnify the standing of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to exalt his seeking of forgiveness, and to point out that his intercession is within the domain of acceptance. The context of the speech would require Him to say: «واستغفرت لهم».

safi-cedvel:65-65.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the meaning of negation in the answer to the oath «[Note: There are many views on the interpretation of the verse, and consequently on the i'rab of (لا): it negates what preceded and is not redundant, the implied meaning being: the matter is not as they claim, that they believe in what was sent down to you; then He began the oath afresh with His saying «وربك لا يؤمنون». Or it is negating and the oath is parenthetical, and the second (لا) is redundant, i.e. «فلا وربك يؤمنون».]»; (الواو) is the wāw of the oath; (رب) is genitive by the wāw, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an implied verb, its implied form being «أقسم», and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (لا) is negating; (يؤمنون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) …, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive; (يحكموا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an «أن» concealed after حتى …, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحكّموك) is in the position of genitive, attached to (يؤمنون).
(في) is a preposition; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (يحكّموك); (شجر) is a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو», and it is the resumptive pronoun (ʿāʾid); (بين) is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative, attached to (شجر), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ثم) is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; (يجدوا) is like يحكّموا, so it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it; (في أنفس) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; (حرجا) is a first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (مما) is like في ما, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of حرج «[Note: Or attached to the maṣdar حرج; and (ما) may be maṣdar-forming, or an indefinite qualified by the clause after it.]»; (قضيت) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn …, and (التاء) is the fāʿil; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يسلموا) is like يحكموا; (تسليما) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «(أقسم) بربك …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يؤمنون» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.
The clause «يحكّموك …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «شجر بينهم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يجدوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يحكّموك.
The clause «قضيت» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «يسلّموا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يحكّموك.

* Morphology:
(حرجا): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb حرج يحرج, of the bāb of فرح; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(تسليما): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb سلّم; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Benefits:
«فَلا وَرَبِّكَ»: The views of the grammarians on the i'rab of «the first لا» are numerous; we summarise them for you as follows:
a- It is a negation of implied speech, i.e. the matter is not as they claim; on this view what follows it is a fresh start.
b- It was placed before the oath out of concern for the negation, then repeated for emphasis.
c- Considering the second «لا» redundant, with the oath intervening between the particle of negation and what is negated, the implied form according to the original order being «فلا يؤمنون وربك».
d- It is redundant and the implied form is «فو ربك», and this redundancy conveys magnification and emphasis.

safi-cedvel:166-166.t:
* I'rab:
(لكن) particle of istidrāk (rectification) with no governing effect, and it was given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters (الله) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) (يشهد) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He) (الباء) preposition (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشهد), (أنزل) past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (إلى) preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل), (أنزل) like the first, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (بعلم) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the third-person pronoun in (أنزله), i.e. «أنزله معلوما» (He sent it down known) [Note: it may be a ḥāl of the fāʿil, i.e. «أنزله عالما به» (He sent it down knowing it).], and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), (الواو) conjunction (الملائكة) mubtadaʾ, nominative (يشهدون) imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (الواو) resumptive (كفى) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif (الباء) redundant (zāʾida) preposition (الله) the Divine Name, genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil of كفى (شهيدا) ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb) [Note: or tamyīz (specification), accusative.].
The clause «الله يشهد ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يشهد ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «أنزل إليك»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أنزله»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or it is explicative of the ṣila clause; it is also said to be a circumstantial clause with قد implied, and it is also said to be parenthetical.].
The clause «الملائكة يشهدون»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يشهدون»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الملائكة).
The clause «كفى بالله ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:167-167.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ (كفروا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (الواو) conjunction (صدّوا) like كفروا (عن سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (صدّوا), (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq) (ضلّوا) like كفروا (ضلالا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) (بعيدا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «إنّ الذين كفروا ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «صدّوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila.
The clause «ضلّوا ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

* Benefits:
His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قَدْ ضَلُّوا ضَلالًا بَعِيداً﴾: قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). The grammarians have views about قد when it enters the past or the imperfect, and they have also cited a number of meanings for it, namely:
1- It conveys expectation (tawaqquʿ), and that is with the imperfect verb, as in your saying قد يقدم الغائب اليوم (the absent one may arrive today), when you expect his arrival. Many have affirmed the meaning of expectation with the past as well. Al-Khalīl said: one says (قد فعل) (he has done) to people who are awaiting the news. And from this is the muezzin's saying قد قامت الصلاة (the prayer has begun), because the congregation is awaiting that. But Ibn Mālik said: in this case it enters an expected past, but it does not itself convey expectation. And this is the truth.
2- Bringing the past near to the present: in your saying قام زيد (Zayd stood) the near or the distant past is possible, whereas your saying قد قام زيد (Zayd has stood) conveys the near past. Hence it was stipulated that it not enter ليس - عسى - نعم - بئس, because they are for the present ... and they are inflexible (jāmid) verbs; and likewise it was stipulated that it enter a past verb occurring as a ḥāl (circumstantial), whether overt, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَما لَنا أَلَّا نُقاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنا مِنْ دِيارِنا﴾, or implied, as in «أَوْ جاؤُكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ», i.e. «قد حصرت صدورهم».
3- Diminution (taqlīl), which is of two kinds: diminishing the occurrence of the action, as in «قد يصدق الكذوب، وقد يجود البخيل» (the liar may sometimes tell the truth, and the miser may sometimes be generous), or diminishing what it relates to, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قَدْ يَعْلَمُ ما أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. what they are upon is the least of the things known to Him, Exalted is He.
4- Multiplication (taksīr): Sībawayh said this regarding the saying of al-Hudhalī:
قد أترك القرن مصفرا أنامله ... كأن أثوابه مجّت بفرصاد
(Often I leave the peer with yellowed fingertips, as though his garments had been spattered with mulberry juice.)
القرن is the one equal in courage, and الفرصاد: the mulberry. Al-Zamakhsharī said regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قَدْ نَرى تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّماءِ﴾, i.e. «ربما نرى» (often We see), and its meaning is the multiplication of seeing.
5- Realization (taḥqīq): this is when it enters the past, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاها وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسَّاها﴾

safi-cedvel:168-169.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ الذين كفروا وظلموا) like its counterpart above [Note: in the previous verse (167).], (لم) particle of negation and jussive (يكن) defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and it was given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters (الله) the Divine Name, noun of يكن, nominative (marfūʿ) (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd) (يغفر) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن after the lām of denial (اللام) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يغفر).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يغفر) is in the position of genitive, attached to the khabar (predicate) of يكن.
(الواو) conjunction (لا) negating, emphasizing the negation (ليهدي) like ليغفر, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (طريقا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يهدي) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to what the first interpreted maṣdar is attached to, for it is conjoined to it.
The clause «إنّ الذين كفروا ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ظلموا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لم يكن الله ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يغفر لهم»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يهديهم ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
(169) (إلّا) particle of exception (طريق) excepted by إلّا, accusative as a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) (جهنّم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote (خالدين) an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial) of the object of يهديهم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (في) preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (خالدين), (أبدا) adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative, attached to خالدين (الواو) resumptive (كان) defective past verb (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as the noun of كان.. and (اللام) is for distance and the kāf for address (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسيرا), which is the khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «كان ذلك ... يسيرا»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:170-170.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) particle of alerting (tanbīh), (الناس) badal (substitute) of أيّ, following it in the nominative in form (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq) (جاء) past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (الرسول) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (بالحقّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of جاء [Note: the bāʾ may be causal, so that the prepositional phrase is attached to the verb جاء, i.e. «جاء بسبب الحقّ» (he came because of the truth).], (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء) [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl of الحقّ.], (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source; آمنوا here is an imperative verb, as the source itself parses the identical form in the next verse] (خيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, for it is its qualifier, i.e. «آمنوا إيمانا خيرا لكم» (believe with a belief that is better for you) [Note: this is the choice of al-Farrāʾ; it may also be a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being ائتوا (bring) or اقصدوا (aim at), which must necessarily be left implicit.], (اللام) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (خيرا), (الواو) conjunction (إن) conditional particle governing the jussive (تكفروا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الفاء) linking the apodosis (إنّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما (الواو) conjunction (الأرض) conjoined to السموات, genitive (majrūr) like it (الواو) resumptive (كان الله عليما حكيما) like كان الله عزيزا حكيما [Note: in verse (165) of this surah.].
The clause «يأيّها الناس ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قد جاءكم الرسول»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «آمنوا»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن دعاكم فآمنوا» (if he calls you, then believe).
The clause «إن تكفروا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ لله ما في السموات»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ; or it is a causal explanation of an implied apodosis, the implied form being «فإنّ الله غني عنكم» (then Allah is free of need of you).
The clause «كان الله عليما ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Benefits:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَآمِنُوا خَيْراً لَكُمْ﴾ — on the i'rab of the word خيرا the statements of the grammarians have diverged, going in various directions of interpretation and implication; we will present them, showing which is closest to correctness.
1- Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said the implied form is وآتوا خيرا [Translator's note: so in the source; the implied verb attributed to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is usually given as ائتوا (bring), as in the note to the i'rab above], so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, because when He commanded them to believe, He wanted to bring them out of one matter and bring them into what is better than it.
2- Some held that it stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the implied form being «فآمنوا إيمانا خيرا» (so believe with a better belief). This is the view of al-Farrāʾ.
3- Al-Kisāʾī holds that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted كان together with its noun, the implied form being «فآمنوا يكن الإيمان خيرا لكم» (so believe; belief will be better for you). This view is not permissible according to the Basrans, because كان is not omitted together with its noun while its khabar remains, except where it is unavoidable. What makes it weaker still is that the implied (يكون) is the apodosis of an omitted condition.
4- It is said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial); this is a weak account. It is evident that the view of the Kufans, considering the word the khabar of an omitted كان together with its noun, suits the meaning and reveals it; but as i'rab it conflicts with the rules of the language, because implication has specific cases, and we cannot give ourselves free rein in this area. The secrets of the Noble Quran and the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, remain above every consideration and too great to be encompassed by any knowledge or penetrated to its core by any human mind. For it is the inimitable speech of Allah.

safi-cedvel:118-119.t:
* I'rab:
(لعن) a past verb; (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) conjunctive «[Note: or circumstantial or resumptive ... and the clause قال is then in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or has no grammatical position, resumptive.]»; (قال) like لعن, and the fāʿil is "huwa", i.e. Satan; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (أتخذنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative ... and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anā"; (من عباد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb (أتخذ), which carries the sense of "I shall make" «[Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl from (نصيبا), or to a second object of the verb اتخذ.]», and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (نصيبا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (مفروضا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «لعنه الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive «[Note: or in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of (شيطانا) in the previous verse (117).]».
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause لعنه الله.
The omitted oath clause «...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «لأتخذن ...» has no grammatical position, the answer of an implied oath.
(الواو) conjunctive; (لأضلّن) like لأتخذن; (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunctive in both places; (لأمنّينّهم، لآمرنهم) like لأضلنهم; (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (يبتكنّ) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, for it is one of the five verbs ...
And the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil, and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis; (آذان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الأنعام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunctive; (لآمرنّهم فليغيرنّ خلق الله) like the preceding; (الواو) resumptive; (من) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يتخذ) an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (الشيطان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (وليّا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتخذ) «[Note: or attached to an omitted naʿt of (وليّا).]»; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) a particle of realization; (خسر) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (خسرانا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (مبينا) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «لأضلّنهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause أتخذن.
The clause «لأمنينهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause أتخذن.
The clause «لآمرنهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause أتخذن.
The clause «يبتّكنّ ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if I command them to slit, then they will surely slit".
The (second) clause «لآمرنهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the first clause لآمرنهم.
The clause «يغيّرنّ ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if I command them to change, then they will surely change".
The clause «من يتخذ ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يتخذ الشيطان ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: it is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of protasis and apodosis together.]».
The clause «خسر ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(خسرانا): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb خسر يخسر, of the bāb فرح, its pattern فعلان with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:120-120.t:
* I'rab:
(يعد) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "long life", and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", i.e. Satan; (الواو) conjunctive; (يمنيهم) like يعدهم, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "the attainment of hopes"; (الواو) circumstantial — or resumptive —; (ما) negating; (يعدهم) like the first; (الشيطان) fāʿil, nominative; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (غرورا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) «[Note: or mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar because it is a kind of it, i.e. "the promise of delusion", or with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "a promise possessing delusion".]».
The clause «يعدهم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يمنيهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause يعدهم.
The clause «ما يعدهم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(غرورا): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb غرّه يغرّه, of the bāb نصر, its pattern فعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ; and there are other maṣdars, namely غر and غرة, with fatḥa on the ghayn in both.

safi-cedvel:121-121.t:
* I'rab:
(أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) ...
and (الكاف) a particle of address; (مأوى) a second mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (جهنم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الواو) conjunctive; (لا) negating; (يجدون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (عن) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (محيصا) «[Note: this is if we take the verb as transitive to one object; if it is taken as transitive to two, the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted second object of the verb, i.e. "they do not find a refuge sufficing or availing them against it".]», which is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
The clause «أولئك مأواهم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «مأواهم جهنم» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «يجدون ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined on the khabar clause.

* Morphology:
(محيصا): a noun of place from حاص يحيص, its pattern مفعل; the word contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by making quiescent: the kasra was heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the ḥāʾ.

safi-cedvel:122-122.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الواو) conjunctive; (عملوا) like آمنوا; (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (السين) a particle of the future; (ندخل) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu", for majesty; (جنّات) a second mafʿūl bihi — by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa) —, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (تجري) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (من تحت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تجري) «[Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأنهار... and in the speech a muḍāf is omitted, i.e. "from beneath its trees".]»; (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الأنهار) fāʿil, nominative; (خالدين) ḥāl, accusative, from the third-person pronoun in (ندخلهم); (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to خالدين; (أبدا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to خالدين. (وعد) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "Allah promised them a promise"; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) ... and this maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasizes the content of the nominal clause before it; (حقا) mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb حق, and this maṣdar emphasizes the content of the promise «[Note: the author of al-Jumal allowed making it a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "made binding" ...]»; (الواو) resumptive; (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أصدق) khabar (predicate), nominative; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أصدق); (قيلا) tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the ṣila clause.
The clause «سندخلهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «تجري ... الأنهار» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات.
The implied clause «(وعد)» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The implied clause «(حق)» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «من أصدق ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(وعد): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb وعد يعد, of the bāb ضرب, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(حقا): an aural maṣdar of the verb حق يحق, of the bāb ضرب, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(أصدق): an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) from صدق, its pattern أفعل.
(قيلا): an aural maṣdar of the verb قال يقول; it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion: its origin is قول; the wāw came quiescent after a kasra, so it was converted to yāʾ ... and (قيل) according to Ibn al-Sikkīt is a noun and not a maṣdar.

safi-cedvel:123-123.t:
* I'rab:
(ليس) an incomplete (nāqiṣ), inflexible (jāmid) past verb, and its noun is omitted, its implied form being "the matter" or "the outcome" «[Note: Abū Ḥayyān chose that the noun be a pronoun referring to the maṣdar understood from His saying سندخلهم, i.e. "entry into Paradise is not by your wishes" ... and it was said that it is a pronoun referring to Allah's promise to the believers of entry into Paradise.]»; (بأمانيّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of ليس, the implied sense being "the matter is not dependent on your wishes" «[Note: it is possible to make the bāʾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and to interpret the noun in a way matching the meaning, i.e. "success through salvation is not wishes of yours".]», and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct);
