(الواو) conjunctive; (لا) redundant, to emphasize the negation; (أماني) maʿṭūf (conjoined) on the first, genitive (majrūr) like it; (أهل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (من) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يعمل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (سوءا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (يجز) an imperfect verb, passive, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يجز); (الواو) conjunctive; (لا) negating; (يجد) an imperfect verb, jussive on (يجز) «[Translator's note: i.e. conjoined on it; the word "conjoined" is missing in the source.]», and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (له) like به, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from وليّ — a naʿt (adjective) that came before what it qualifies —; (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from (وليّا); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (وليّا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunctive; (لا) redundant, to emphasize the negation; (نصيرا) conjoined on (وليّا), accusative like it.
The clause «ليس ... بأمانيكم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «من يعمل ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يعمل سوءا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: it is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of protasis and apodosis together.]».
The clause «يجز به» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا يجد ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the apodosis clause.

* Morphology:
(أمانيّ): plural of أمنية, a noun for what a person seeks to be realized; its verb is منى يمني, of the bāb ضرب; its pattern is أفعيلة with ḍamma on the hamza, and the pattern of أمانيّ is أفاعيل.
(يجز): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion due to the jussive; its pattern is يفع.

* Benefits:
Deeds are the measure:
The Jews and the Christians used to say: ﴿نَحْنُ أَبْناءُ اللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ﴾ ("We are the sons of Allah and His beloved"), and they used to say: ﴿لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّاماً مَعْدُوداتٍ﴾ ("The Fire will not touch us except for a number of days").. And the Jews used to say, and still say, that they are Allah's chosen people.
And perhaps some Muslims, too, entertained in their souls the idea that they are the best community brought forth for mankind, and that Allah overlooks what occurs from them because they are the Muslims.
So this text came to return these people to deeds alone, and to return all people to a single scale, which is submitting one's face to Allah, together with excellence (iḥsān), and following Islam, the creed of Abraham before, Abraham whom Allah took as an intimate friend.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(يريد) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (اللام) redundant (zāʾida); (يبيّن) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by a concealed (أن) after the lām, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يبيّن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبيّن) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being (يريد) ... as for the near position, it is the genitive by the lām [Note: some make this lām a preposition of cause, with the object of (يريد) implied, i.e. "Allah wants the making clear, in order to make clear" ... The i'rab we have adopted is the more analogical.].
(الواو) conjunctive; (يهدي) an imperfect verb, accusative, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the verb (يبيّن), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (سنن) the second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (يتوب) like (يهدي); (عليكم) like (لكم), attached to (يتوب), (الواو) resumptive; (الله عليم حكيم) like (الله غفور رحيم) in the preceding verse.
The clause «يريد الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يبين لكم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يهديكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (يبين لكم).
The clause «يتوب عليكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (يبين لكم).
The clause «الله عليم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:27-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (يريد) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يتوب عليكم) its i'rab was given in the preceding verse.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتوب ...) is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being (يريد).
(الواو) conjunctive; (يريد) like the first; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; (يتبعون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الشهوات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (أن) like the first; (تميلوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (ميلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (عظيما) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تميلوا ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being the second (يريد).
The clause «الله يريد ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the preceding verse.
The clause «يريد أن يتوب» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «يتوب عليكم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يريد الذين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (الله يريد).
The clause «يتبعون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «تميلوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
(يريد) like the first; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (أن يخفّف عنكم) like (أن يتوب عليكم); (الواو) resumptive; (خلق) a passive past verb; (الإنسان) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (ضعيفا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative.
The clause «يريد الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يخفف عنكم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «خلق الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal.

* Morphology:
(الشهوات): plural of الشهوة, an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb شها يشهو, of the bāb of نصر, and شهي يشهي, of the bāb of فرح; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn, and the pattern of the plural is فعلات with two fatḥas.
(ميلا): the maṣdar of مال يميل, of the bāb of ضرب; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; and the verb has other maṣdars: تميال with fatḥa on the tāʾ, ميلان on the pattern فعلان with two fatḥas, ميلولة, ممال with two fatḥas, and مميل with fatḥa on the first letter.

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative (manṣūb), and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a badal (substitute) of (أي) or a naʿt (adjective) of it; (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (لا) the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā; (تأكلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أموال) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أموال) [Note: it may be attached to the verb (تأكلوا).] (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (بالباطل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the agent of (تأكلوا) [Note: or to a ḥāl of (أموال), i.e. "extracted [Translator's note: the source prints «مستحلصة», evidently for «مستخلصة».] by falsehood" ... or attached to the verb], i.e. "being engaged in falsehood"; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (تكون) a defective imperfect verb, accusative, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it", i.e. the wealth; (تجارة) khabar (predicate), accusative; (عن تراض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of (تجارة), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ dropped because of the tanwīn, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to an omitted naʿt of (تراض).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون ...) is in the position of the accusative by disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because trade is other than the wealth consumed by falsehood.
(الواو) conjunctive; (لا تقتلوا أنفسكم) like (لا تأكلوا أموالكم); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (كان) a defective past verb, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (بكم) like (منكم), attached to (رحيما), which is the khabar of kāna, accusative.
The vocative clause «يا ايها الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا تأكلوا ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «تكون تجارة» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «لا تقتلوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ الله كان ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal.
The clause «كان بكم رحيما» is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar of (إنّ).

* Morphology:
(تراض): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the five-letter verb تراضى; it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion on account of the tanwīn; its pattern is تفاعل, on the pattern of the past tense, with the alif converted to a yāʾ and the letter before it given kasra.

* Rhetoric:
Synecdoche-type metonymy (al-majāz al-mursal) [Translator's note: the source prints «المجازر المرسل», evidently for «المجاز المرسل».]: in His saying, Exalted is He: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْباطِلِ, i.e. do not take your wealth by unlawful means such as usury, gambling and the like. He expressed it by "eating" because it is caused by the taking, so the relation is that of causation.

* Benefits:
1- Lawful earning:
He, Blessed and Exalted is He, forbids His believing servants from consuming one another's wealth by falsehood, i.e. by illegitimate means such as usury, gambling, fraud, bribery, and hoarding goods to raise their prices, and likewise all kinds of forbidden sales — «except that it be trade by mutual consent among you». This is a disconnected exception, as if He were saying: do not engage in forbidden means of acquiring wealth; but lawful trading, which takes place by mutual consent of seller and buyer — use that as a means of obtaining wealth.
2- The option of the two parties to a sale:
Part of complete mutual consent is enjoying the option of the session (khiyār al-majlis), as is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs,
his saying ﷺ: «When two men conclude a sale, each of them has the option as long as they have not separated».
Aḥmad and al-Shāfiʿī, their followers, and the majority of the early and later generations adopted this view on the basis of this ḥadīth. Among this is the legitimacy of the option of stipulation (khiyār al-sharṭ) after the contract, up to three days.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يفعل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (عدوانا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "transgressing and wronging".], (الواو) conjunctive; (ظلما) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (عدوانا), accusative like it; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (سوف) a particle of the future; (نصلي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (الهاء) a pronoun, the first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We", for majesty; (نارا) the second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) resumptive; (كان) a defective past verb; (ذلك) like the first, the noun of kāna, the reference being to the burning; (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسيرا), which is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative.
The clause «من يفعل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «يفعل ذلك ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «سوف نصليه نارا» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كان ذلك ... يسيرا» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(يسيرا): a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from يسر ييسر, of the bāb of كرم; its pattern is فعيل.

* Benefits:
1- The difference of form caused by the hamza of transitivity.
a- The majority read «نصليه» with ḍamma on the nūn, the reason being the entry of «the hamza of transitivity» into the verb, so its ruling became that of the quadriliteral.
b- Others considered the verb to be triliteral and read «نصليه» with fatḥa on the nūn, because it is from صلى يصلي ...
2- Between the protasis and its apodosis:
The grammarians differed about the khabar when the conditional noun is a mubtadaʾ — which of them is the khabar: the protasis, or its apodosis, or both together.
There are three views. The most preponderant of them is that the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar, because the meaning is not complete except by mentioning them together, and the khabar is the speech that completes the meaning.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) a jussive conditional particle; (تجتنبوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (كبائر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (تنهون) a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (عن) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تنهون), (نكفّر) an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "We", for majesty; (عنكم) like (عنه), attached to (نكفّر), (سيئات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (ندخل) like (نكفّر) and conjoined to it, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "We"; (مدخلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative [Note: it may be a mafʿūl bihi, by its being a noun of place, not a mīmī maṣdar.. and if it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, the mafʿūl bihi is implied, i.e. "We shall admit you to Paradise" ...], (كريما) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «تجتنبوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تنهون عنه» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «نكفّر عنكم ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ندخلكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (نكفر عنكم).

* Morphology:
(كبائر): plural of كبيرة, the feminine of كبير, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective); its pattern is فعيل and فعيلة.
(مدخلا): a mīmī maṣdar from the quadriliteral verb أدخل; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn ... and in the verse it may be a noun of place on the same pattern.
(كريما): a ṣifa mushabbaha from the verb كرم يكرم — the fifth bāb —; its pattern is فعيل.

* Benefits:
1- The seven major sins:
It is reported from Ṣuhayb, the client of «al-Ṣawārī», that he heard Abū Hurayra and Abū Saʿīd saying: «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us one day and said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul" three times; then he bent down, and every man among us bent down weeping, not knowing what he had sworn about. Then he raised his head, and on his face was good tidings, which was dearer to us than red camels. He said: "There is no servant who prays the five prayers, fasts Ramaḍān, pays the zakāt and avoids the seven major sins, but the gates of Paradise are opened for him, and then it is said to him: Enter in peace"».
Many ḥadīths have come mentioning the seven major sins, among them what is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Avoid the seven destructive sins. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, and what are they? He said: "Associating partners with Allah, killing the soul that Allah has forbidden except by right, sorcery, consuming usury, consuming the property of the orphan, turning away on the day of the advance, and slandering chaste, unaware, believing women"».

safi-cedvel:171-171.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle (أهل) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb) (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (لا) prohibitive, governing the jussive (تغلوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (في دين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تغلوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (لا تقولوا) like لا تغلوا (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحقّ, i.e. «موقوفا أو منطبقا على الله» (restricted to, or applying to, Allah) (إلّا) particle of restriction (الحقّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: it may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is a kind of it.], (إنّما) the restraining [mā] and the restrained [particle] (kāffa wa-makfūfa) (المسيح) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) (عيسى) badal (substitute) of المسيح, nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif (ابن) naʿt (adjective) of عيسى, nominative like it, or a badal of it (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, since it is a diptote (رسول) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ المسيح, nominative (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) conjunction (كلمة) conjoined to رسول, nominative like it, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (ألقى) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He) (إلى مريم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ألقى), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa (الواو) conjunction (روح) conjoined to رسول, nominative like it (من) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt of روح. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (آمنوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنوا), (الواو) conjunction (رسل) conjoined to the Divine Name, genitive like it, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (لا تقولوا) like the first (ثلاثة) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being الآلهة (the gods) (انتهوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (خيرا لكم) like آمنوا خيرا لكم in the previous verse (إنما الله) like إنّما المسيح (إله) khabar of the mubtadaʾ الله (واحد) naʿt of إله, nominative like it (سبحانه) mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle (يكون) defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative [Note: or it is complete (tāmm), and (له) is attached to (يكون) or is a ḥāl of ولد.. and ولد is its fāʿil.], (اللام) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the fronted khabar of (يكون), (ولد) the postponed noun of يكون, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكون له ولد) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, the implied form being «عن أن يكون ...» (above having ...), attached to سبحان.
(له) like the first, attached to a fronted khabar (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما (الواو) conjunction (ما في الأرض) like the preceding one and conjoined to it (الواو) conjunction (كفى) past verb (الباء) redundant (zāʾida) preposition (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil in position, genitive in form (وكيلا) ḥāl, accusative [Note: or tamyīz (specification), accusative.].
The clause «يا أهل الكتاب ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا تغلوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «لا تقولوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «إنّما المسيح ... رسول الله»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), or explicative of the content of الحقّ.
The clause «ألقاها ...»: in the position of accusative, a ḥāl of (كلمته), with قد implied.
The clause «آمنوا»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: «ان صدّقتم ذلك فآمنوا» (if you believe that, then believe).
The clause «لا تقولوا (the second)»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause آمنوا بالله.
The clause «(الآلهة) ثلاثة»: in the position of accusative, the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «انتهوا»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّما الله إله ...»: has no grammatical position, giving the reason for the demand to desist.
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحانه..»: has no grammatical position, parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «يكون له ولد»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «له ما في السموات»: has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal: it gives the reason for the declaration of transcendence.
The clause «كفى بالله وكيلا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause له ما في السموات.

* Benefits:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ — it is to be noted that the hamza of ابن has been retained, because the grammarians stipulated for its omission that it occur between two proper names, the second of which is the father of the first, whereas here the second name is the name of a mother. It is well known that the hamza of (ابن) and (ابنة) is omitted when it occurs between two proper names and is intended as a description, and in this case the proper name before it may not take tanwīn, as in our saying خالد بن الوليد سيف الله المسلول (Khālid ibn al-Walīd is the drawn sword of Allah). Here the hamza of ابن has been omitted and the word خالد may not take tanwīn. But if it occurs between two proper names and is intended as an informing statement (ikhbār), its hamza is retained and the proper name before it must take tanwīn; so I say, in answer to someone who asks me «عليّ ابن من؟» (ʿAlī is whose son?): «عليّ ابن أبي طالب» (ʿAlī is the son of Abū Ṭālib). Here it occurred between two proper names and was intended as an informing statement, so the proper name before it had to take tanwīn and its hamza was retained. Likewise, if it occurs between a proper name and something that is not a proper name, its hamza is retained, as in my saying: أنا ابن علي (I am the son of ʿAlī) or علي ابن الكرام (ʿAlī is the son of noble people). Likewise its hamza is retained whenever it occurs at the beginning of a line, absolutely.

safi-cedvel:66-68.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction; (لو أنّا) is like لو أنهم «[Note: In verse (64) of this sūra.]»; (كتبنا) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn …, and (نا) is the fāʿil (agent); (على) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (كتبنا); (أن) is an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr); (اقتلوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أنفس) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أو) is a conjunction; (اخرجوا) is like اقتلوا; (من ديار) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اخرجوا), and (كم) is a muḍāf ilayhi; (ما) is negating; (فعلوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (إلا) is a particle of exception; (قليل) is a badal (substitute) of the agent pronoun in (فعلوه), nominative (marfūʿ); (منهم) is like عليهم, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of قليل; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لو أنّهم): its i'rab has already been given «[Note: In verse (64) of this sūra.]»; (فعلوا) is like the first; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; (يوعظون) is an imperfect verb, passive, nominative, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الباء) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يوعظون); (اللام) occurs in the apodosis of لو; (كان) is a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو», i.e. the doing understood from the context of the verse; (خيرا) is the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative; (لهم) is like به, attached to (خيرا); (الواو) is a conjunction; (أشد) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the khabar of كان, accusative; (تثبيتا) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «(ثبتت) كتابتنا عليهم» is a clause with no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «كتبنا عليهم …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «اقتلوا» has no grammatical position, explicative «[Note: (أن) may be a maṣdar-forming particle, and it together with the verb after it is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi governed by كتبنا … In the i'rab above the object is implied.]».
The clause «اخرجوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the explicative clause.
The clause «ما فعلوه …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «(ثبت) فعلهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «فعلوا …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «يوعظون به» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «كان خيرا …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(67) (الواو) is a conjunction; (إذا) is a particle of response; (اللام) occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «لو ثبتوا لآتيناهم»; (آتينا) is like كتبنا, and (هم) is the first mafʿūl bihi; (من) is a preposition; (لدن) is a noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of genitive, attached to (آتينا), and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أجرا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (عظيما) is a naʿt, accusative.
The clause «آتيناهم …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition … and إذا — with tanwīn — together with what lies in its scope, namely the conditional particle, its verb and its apodosis, has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause «[Note: This last sentence, consisting of the particle of response and the implied condition, may be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), and that is the choice of al-Zamakhsharī.]».
(68) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لهديناهم) is like لآتيناهم; (صراطا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, governed by هدينا; (مستقيما) is a naʿt, accusative.
The clause «هديناهم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتيناهم.

* Benefits:
The religion of ease:
This way (manhaj) is made easy so that everyone of sound innate nature (fiṭra) can rise to it. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, who imposed on man the obligations of this religion, knows that they are within man's capacity, and He did not legislate this religion for the distinguished few among people. Killing oneself and leaving one's homes … are two examples of arduous obligations which, had they been prescribed for people, none but a few of them would have done; and they were not prescribed, because the aim of obligations is not that people in general be incapable of them or shrink back from them; rather, the aim is that all be able to do them and discharge them.
This does not preclude the existence of an elite distinguished by the depth of its faith and the strength of its bond with Allah, Glorified be He.
Ibn Jurayj said: al-Muthannā Isḥāq Abū al-Azhar narrated to us from Ismāʿīl from Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī, who said: When وَلَوْ أَنَّا كَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنِ اقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ ... (the verse) was revealed, a man said: "Had we been commanded, we would have done it; and praise be to Allah who has spared us." That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: «Among my community are men in whose hearts faith is firmer than the firmly-rooted mountains.»

safi-cedvel:69-69.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يطع) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), given kasra because two sukūns met, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) is a conjunction; (الرسول) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, accusative like it; (الفاء) links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (أولاء) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (الكاف) is for address; (مع) is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أولاء); (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أنعم) is a past verb; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (على) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنعم); (من النبييّن) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the third-person pronoun in (عليهم), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (الصدّيقين، الشهداء، الصالحين) are nouns conjoined to النبيين by conjunctions, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive for the masculine plural being the yāʾ; (الواو) is resumptive; (حسن) is a past verb; (أولئك) is like the first, and it is the fāʿil; (رفيقا) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «من يطع الله …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يطع الله …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «أولئك مع الذين …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أنعم الله …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «حسن أولئك …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الصدّيقين): plural of الصدّيق, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from صدق يصدق, of the bāb of نصر; its pattern is فعيّل with kasra on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn.
(رفيقا): a ṣifa mushabbaha, its pattern being فعيل, from رفق يرفق, of the bāb of نصر, the bāb of كرم and the bāb of فرح; singular and plural may be equal in it, and in the verse it can be interpreted in the sense of the plural, i.e. رفقاء, or as: each one of these four kinds is a companion «[Note: In al-Jamal's gloss (ḥāshiya) on the Jalālayn: «… He made الرفيق singular although it describes a plural because the Arabs use it for the singular and the plural … and it is said its meaning is: and how excellent is each one of those as a companion».]».

* Benefits:
1- Pay attention to the spelling of «أولئك»:
a- The «wāw» in it is written but not pronounced.
b- The alif occurring after the lām, conversely, is pronounced but not written.
2- Obedience to the Messenger is frequently mentioned in the Noble Qurʾān coupled with obedience to Allah, and in that is an indication of the place of the Sunna in legislation, and that it comes in second rank among the sources of legislation.

safi-cedvel:70-70.t:
* I'rab:
(ذا) is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الفضل) is a badal (substitute) of ذا or a naʿt (adjective) of it, following it in the nominative «[Note: It may be the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, with the preposition and its genitive noun after it attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it.]»; (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (الواو) is resumptive; (كفى) is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الباء) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil (agent) of كفى; (عليما) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb), or a ḥāl, accusative.
The clause «ذلك الفضل من الله» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفى بالله عليما» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) is a vocative particle; (أي) is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of أي or a naʿt (adjective) of it; (آمنوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma …, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (خذوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn …, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (حذر) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (انفروا) is like خذوا; (ثبات) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra «[Note: What permitted the ḥāl to come as a non-derived (jāmid) word is that it is interpreted as a derived one, i.e. «متفرقين» (in separate groups).]»; (أو) is a conjunction; (انفروا جميعا) is like انفروا ثبات.
The vocative clause «يا أيها الذين …» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «خذوا …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «انفروا ثبات» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «انفروا جميعا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.

* Morphology:
(حذركم): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb حذر; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn. (ثبات): plural of ثبة, a collective noun (ism jamʿ), said to be more than ten or more than two; its pattern is فعة with ḍamma on the fāʾ and deletion of the final radical, which is most likely the wāw, because the verb is ثبا يثبو; some say it is the yāʾ, because it is from the verb «ثبيت على الرجل» when you praise him … It is pluralised with alif and tāʾ — as in the verse — and with wāw and nūn.

* Rhetoric:
«خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ» …
Caution is guarding against what is feared; so there is kināya (metonymy) and takhyīl (imaginative depiction) by likening caution to weapons and an instrument of protection.

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (من يقتل مؤمنا) like the previous [Note: in the previous verse (92)..] , (متعمدا) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of يقتل; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (جزاء) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (جهنم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (خالدا) an accusative ḥāl of something implied [Note: It is the object pronoun of a verb whose implied form is: جازاه الله خالدا فيها ("Allah requites him, abiding in it") ... or of the object pronoun or deputy-agent pronoun of a verb whose implied form is: يجزاها خالدا فيها ("he is requited with it, abiding in it") ... It is weak for it to be a ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in His saying (جزاؤه), for two reasons: the first, that it is a muḍāf ilayhi; and the second, that the ḥāl and its owner would be separated by something foreign, namely the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.] , (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خالدا); (الواو) conjunction; (غضب) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (غضب); (الواو) conjunction; (لعنه) a verb and its object, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (الواو) conjunction; (أعدّ) like غضب; (له) like عليه, attached to (أعدّ); (عذابا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (عظيما) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «من يقتل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما كان لمؤمن [Note: in the previous verse (92).] .
The clause «يقتل مؤمنا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.] The clause «جزاؤه جهنم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «غضب الله عليه» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: جزاه الله وغضب عليه ("Allah requited him and was angry with him").
The clause «لعنه» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied resumptive clause. The clause «أعدّ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(متعمدا): an active participle from the five-letter تعمد; its pattern is متفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
- In this verse there is a beautiful and original device, the device of murāʿāt al-naẓīr (congruence of associated terms):
It is that the speaker brings what suits the content. The verse is filled with words indicating severe threat and firm warning, and with kinds of thunder and lightning, to indicate that the crime of killing is one of the greatest of crimes and the most deeply sunk in evil.

* Benefits:
The prohibition of killing: killing, when it is intentional and aggressive, is a major crime and one of the seven destructive sins, which entail deserving punishment in this world and the Hereafter — that is, by retaliation (qiṣāṣ), and by abiding eternally in the fire of Hell — because it is an assault on the work of Allah on earth and a threat to the security of the community and the life of society.

safi-cedvel:94-94.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أي) the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of أي or a naʿt (adjective) of it; (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إذا) an adverb for future time containing the sense of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis; (ضربتم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn ...
and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of ضربتم [Note: i.e. striving in the way of Allah.] , (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (تبينوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā that makes the verb jussive; (تقولوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (اللام) a preposition; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (تقولوا); (ألقى) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (إلى) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (ألقى); (السلام) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (لست) an inflexible (jāmid), incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb ... and (التاء) a pronoun in the position of nominative as the noun of ليس; (مؤمنا) the khabar (predicate) of ليس, accusative; (تبتغون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (عرض) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الحياة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الدنيا) naʿt of الحياة, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being an implied kasra on the alif; (الفاء) giving the reason (taʿlīliyya); (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to a fronted khabar; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (مغانم) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (كثيرة) naʿt, nominative. (الكاف) a preposition and (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to the omitted fronted khabar of the incomplete verb, and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (كنتم) an incomplete past verb, indeclinable on sukūn ... and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of كان; (من) a preposition; (قبل) a noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to the omitted khabar; (الفاء) conjunction; (من) a past verb [Translator's note: i.e. مَنَّ, printed in the source without the shadda]; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (عليكم) like إليكم, attached to (منّ); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (تبيّنوا) like the first; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (كان) an incomplete past verb, its noun a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive [Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle ... and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive, attached to (خبيرا).] , attached to (خبيرا), and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted; (تعلمون) like تبتغون; (خبيرا) the khabar of كان, accusative.
The vocative clause «يا أيها الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ضربتم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تبينوا» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition ... and the condition, with its verb and its apodosis, is the reply to the vocative.
The clause «لا تقولوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «ألقى ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «لست مؤمنا» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تبتغون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of تقولوا.
The clause «عند الله مغانم ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) or giving the reason.
The clause «كنتم من قبل» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «منّ الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كنتم ...
The clause «تبيّنوا» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. إن أنعم الله عليكم فتبيّنوا نعمة الله ("if Allah has bestowed favour on you, then recognize clearly the favour of Allah").
The clause «إن الله كان ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «كان ... خبيرا» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تعلمون ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما).

* Morphology:
(عرض) an inflexible (jāmid) noun meaning goods, or a noun for what has no permanence; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(مغانم): the plural of مغنم, a noun meaning booty; it is in the form of the mīm-maṣdar of the verb غنم يغنم, of the class of فرح.

safi-cedvel:95-95.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative; (يستوي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ; (القاعدون) fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (من المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (القاعدون); (غير) a badal (substitute) of (القاعدون), nominative like it [Note: Or a naʿt (adjective) of it, because القاعدين is not fully definite and no specific people are meant by it, and because the (أل) in it is generic.] , (أولي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, since it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (الضرر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (المجاهدون) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (القاعدون), nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (المجاهدون); (الله) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (بأموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (المجاهدون), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (أنفسهم) maʿṭūf to أموالهم ...
and a muḍāf ilayhi. (فضّل) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (المجاهدين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (بأموالهم وأنفسهم) like the first, and attached to المجاهدين; (على القاعدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فضّل), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (درجة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its number or kind, i.e. a preference of one degree, or the preference of a degree [Note: It may be a ḥāl on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. ذوي درجة ("possessing a degree"), or accusative by removal of the preposition, the original being بدرجة.] , (الواو) parenthetical; (كلا) a fronted mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (وعد الله) like فضّل الله; (الحسنى) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being an implied fatḥa on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (فضّل الله المجاهدين على القاعدين) like the first; (أجرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, since it coincides with the verb in meaning, i.e. أجره أجرا عظيما ("He rewarded him with a great reward") [Note: Or accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. فضلهم بأجر ("He preferred them with a reward").] , (عظيما) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «لا يستوي القاعدون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «فضل الله المجاهدين» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «وعد الله ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical.
The clause «فضل الله (the second)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the first clause فضّل.

* Morphology:
(القاعدون): the plural of القاعد, an active participle from قعد يقعد; its pattern is فاعل.
(الضرر): a maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb ضرّ يضرّ, of the class of نصر; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(المجاهدون): the plural of المجاهد, an active participle from the four-letter جاهد; its pattern is مفاعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(الحسنى): a derived noun, the feminine of الأحسن; its pattern is فعلى, with ḍamma then sukūn; or Paradise is meant by it, in which case it is not derived.
(أجرا): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb أجر يأجر, of the class of نصر and the class of ضرب; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
1- The merit of those who strive:
فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجاهِدِينَ بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَلَى الْقاعِدِينَ دَرَجَةً.
In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «In Paradise there are a hundred degrees which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His way; between every two degrees is as between heaven and earth» «وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى» .
Faith has its weight and value in every case, while its people differ in degrees according to their differing in carrying out the obligations of faith, with regard to striving with wealth and lives ... and this qualification is what makes us understand that these who sit back are not the dawdling hypocrites mentioned previously in this context.
2- The saying of Allah the Exalted غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ — opinions have conflicted on the i'rab of the word «غير» in several ways:
a- The first case is «the nominative», as an adjective of «القاعدون» or a badal of «القاعدون» .
b- There is a reading with the accusative, according to which the word «غير» is parsed as an exception from القاعدين, or from المؤمنين, or as a ḥāl ... !
c- And there is a reading with the genitive, according to which «غير» is parsed as an adjective of المؤمنين.
3- The saying of Allah the Exalted: أَجْراً عَظِيماً.
The grammarians took various positions on the i'rab of the word «اجرا» .
a- Standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq, because the meaning of «فضلهم» is «آجرهم» ("He rewarded them").
b- Mafʿūl bihi, because «فضّلهم» means «أعطاهم» ("He gave them").
c- Accusative by removal of the preposition, on the implied form بـ«أجر». The first view is the strongest of these views, and Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:96-96.t:
* I'rab:
(درجات) a badal (substitute) of (أجرا), following it in the accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of درجات; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (مغفرة، رحمة) two nouns conjoined to درجات, accusative like it [Note: مغفرة may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb ...] , (الواو) conjunction; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of كان, nominative; (غفورا) the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative; (رحيما) a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «كان الله غفورا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:172-172.t:
* I'rab:
(لن) particle of negation and accusative (يستنكف) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) (المسيح) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle (يكون) imperfect verb, accusative, defective (nāqiṣ), and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he) (عبدا) khabar (predicate) of يكون, accusative (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (عبدا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكون) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (يستنكف), the implied form being: «عن أن يكون ...» (from being ...).
(الواو) conjunction (لا) redundant (zāʾida), for emphasizing the negation (الملائكة) conjoined to المسيح, nominative like it (المقرّبون) naʿt of الملائكة, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (الواو) conjunction (من) conditional noun governing the jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (يستنكف) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (عن عبادة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يستنكف), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (يستكبر) like يستنكف, and conjoined to it (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) (السين) particle of the future (يحشر) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: the pronoun in (يستنكف) is singular, referring to the form of (من), while the third-person pronoun in (سيحشرهم) refers to the meaning of (من), or to the meaning of "whoever disdains and whoever does not disdain"; so there is an implied element required by the context of the noble verse.], (إلى) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يحشر), (جميعا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the hāʾ in His saying يحشرهم.
The clause «لن يستنكف المسيح....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أن يكون ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن). The clause «من يستنكف ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يستنكف ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «يستكبر»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يستنكف.
The clause «يحشرهم»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(المقرّبون): plural of المقرّب, the passive participle of the quadriliteral قرّب; and from it [is the pattern] مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(عبادة): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of عبد يعبد, of the naṣara class; its pattern is فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ. There are other maṣdars of the verb, namely عبودة, عبوديّة, and معبد with fatḥa on the mīm and the bāʾ, and likewise معبدة.

* Rhetoric:
Concision by omission (al-ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf): in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿لَا الْمَلائِكَةُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾
for «عبادا لله» (servants of Allah) has been omitted, i.e. «ولا الملائكة المقربون أن يكونوا عبادا لله» (nor the angels brought near [disdain] to be servants of Allah); this was omitted because «[عَ]بْداً لِلَّهِ» indicates it [Translator's note: the source text here is garbled («لدلالةَبْداً لِلَّهِ»); it evidently means «لدلالة «عَبْداً لِلَّهِ» عليه», i.e. because the earlier words «عبدا لله» indicate it], for concision..

safi-cedvel:173-173.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction of consequence (tafrīʿiyya) (أمّا) particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl) (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (الواو) conjunction (عملوا) like آمنوا (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra (الفاء) linking the answer of أمّا (يوفّي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", i.e. Allah, and (هم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (أجور) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (يزيدهم) like يوفّيهم (من فضل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يزيد), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (أمّا الذين ... فيعذّبهم) parsed like the preceding (عذابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, for it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar), accusative (أليما) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «الذين آمنوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من يستنكف.. [Note: in the previous verse (172).].
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يوفّيهم ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «يزيدهم ...»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يوفّيهم.
The clause «الذين استنكفوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause الذين آمنوا.
The clause «استنكفوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «استكبروا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استنكفوا.
The clause «يعذّبهم»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (الذين).
(الواو) conjunction (لا) negating (يجدون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (اللام) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يجدون) [Note: or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يجدون, on the view that it is transitive to two objects, the first object being (وليّا).], (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (وليّا) — a naʿt that has come before the qualified noun — (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (وليّا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) conjunction (لا) redundant (zāʾida), for emphasizing the negation, (نصيرا) conjoined to (وليّا), accusative like it.
The clause «لا يجدون ...»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يعذّبهم.

* Benefits:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ — أمّا is parsed as a particle of condition and detailing; we will present some of the grammarians' views about it:
1- It is a particle of condition, detailing and emphasis. As for condition, the evidence is that the fāʾ must follow it, as evidenced by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلا تَقْهَرْ﴾. As for detailing, it is the predominant of its states, as in His saying, Exalted is He:
﴿أَمَّا السَّفِينَةُ فَكانَتْ لِمَساكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِي الْبَحْرِ﴾. It may come with no detailing at all, as in: أما زيد فمنطلق (as for Zayd, he is departing). As for emphasis, al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it and explained it thoroughly, for he said: the benefit of (أما) in speech is that it gives it extra emphasis; you say زيد ذاهب (Zayd is going), and if you intend to emphasize that, and that he is inevitably going, you say: أما زيد فذاهب (as for Zayd, he is going). That is why Sībawayh said in his explanation of this sentence: «مهما يكن من شيء فزيد ذاهب» (whatever may be the case, Zayd is going). This explanation indicates two benefits: its being emphasis, and the meaning of condition.
2- His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أَمَّا ذا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — أمّا here is originally the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) أم and the interrogative ما, and the mīm was assimilated into the mīm because they are identical.

safi-cedvel:174-174.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أيها.. برهان) its i'rab has been given before [Note: in verse (170) of this surah.], (من ربّكم) a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of برهان [Note: or attached to (جاءكم).], (الواو) conjunction (أنزلنا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (نا) is the fāʿil (agent) (إلى) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزلنا), (نورا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (مبينا) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «يا ايّها الناس ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قد جاءكم برهان»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أنزلنا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.

* Morphology:
(برهان): a noun meaning "proof" (al-ḥujja), from the quadriliteral verb برهن; its pattern is فعلان with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:175-175.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (أمّا الذين آمنوا بالله واعتصموا به) the i'rab of its counterpart has been given before [Note: in verse (173) of this surah; and in the speech there is an omission dispensed with because of what is mentioned, i.e.: «وأمّا الذين كفروا فلهم كذا وكذا....» (and as for those who disbelieved, for them is such and such ...).], (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) (السين) particle of the future (يدخل) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", i.e. Allah (في رحمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يدخلهم), (من) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة (الواو) conjunction (فضل) conjoined to رحمة, genitive (majrūr) like it (الواو) conjunction (يهديهم) like يدخلهم (إليه) like منه, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (صراطا) — a naʿt that has come before the qualified noun — (صراطا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) (مستقيما) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «أمّا الذين آمنوا ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اعتصموا به»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «سيدخلهم..»: in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين).
The clause «يهديهم»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause سيدخلهم.

* Rhetoric:
Al-majāz al-mursal (non-metaphorical trope): in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَسَيُدْخِلُهُمْ فِي رَحْمَةٍ﴾, because a human being does not dwell within mercy, since it is an abstract notion; rather he dwells in its place, which is Paradise.
So using "mercy" for its place is a trope in which the thing that dwells is mentioned and the place where it dwells is meant; its relation is thus that of the dwelling thing (al-ḥāliyya).

safi-cedvel:124-124.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (من يعمل) its i'rab has passed «[Note: in the previous verse (123).]»; (من الصالحات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "something of the righteous deeds" «[Note: or attached to (يعمل), and من is partitive.]»; (من ذكر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of يعمل; (أو) a conjunction; (أنثى) maʿṭūf (conjoined) on ذكر, genitive (majrūr) like it, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) circumstantial; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (مؤمن) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (الكاف) a particle of address; (يدخلون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الجنة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunctive; (لا) negating; (يظلمون) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative ... and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (نقيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they will not be wronged a wrong the measure of a speck".
The clause «من يعمل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the previous clause من يعمل «[Note: in the previous verse (123).]».
The clause «يعمل ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «هو مؤمن» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «أولئك يدخلون» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يدخلون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «لا يظلمون ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined on the clause يدخلون الجنة.

* Morphology:
(نقيرا): a noun for the hollow found in the date-stone; it is فعيل in the sense of مفعول (al-Nisāʾ 55).

safi-cedvel:125-125.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أحسن) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (دينا) tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb); (من) a preposition; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أحسن; (أسلم) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (وجه) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسلم); (الواو) circumstantial; (هو محسن) like هو مؤمن «[Note: in the previous verse (124).]»; (الواو) conjunctive; (اتبع) like أسلم; (ملة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (إبراهيم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (حنيفا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from إبراهيم «[Note: or from the fāʿil of اتبع.]»; (الواو) resumptive; (اتخذ) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (إبراهيم) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (خليلا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «من أحسن ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أسلم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «هو محسن» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «اتبع ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the ṣila clause.
The clause «اتخذ الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
«وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْراهِيمَ خَلِيلًا» is a figurative expression (majāz) for His choosing him and singling him out with an honour resembling the honour a friend has with his friend. It is a parenthetical clause whose benefit is to emphasize the obligation of following his creed, because one who reached such nearness to Allah that he was taken as an intimate friend is worthy of having his creed and way followed.

* Benefits:
1- ممّن with shadda:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ دِيناً مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ﴾ — its origin is «من من»; the nūn was assimilated into the mīm, so it was written as a doubled mīm.
2- His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ﴾ contains a fine and subtle point, in that He singled out the face for submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because of what it contains of hearing, sight, intellect and the rest of the senses; it is like the reins of a person, so if this organ submits, the rest of the organs follow it and are led by its commands and prohibitions. This is among the secrets of eloquence and clarity and the utmost precision in the noble Quranic expression.

safi-cedvel:126-126.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (الواو) conjunctive; (ما) like the first and maʿṭūf (conjoined) on it; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila of the second ما; (الواو) conjunctive; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of kāna, nominative (marfūʿ); (بكل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (محيطا); (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (محيطا) the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb).
The clause «لله ما في السموات» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the previous resumptive clause «[Note: in verse (125).]».
The clause «كان الله ... محيطا» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause لله ما في السموات.

safi-cedvel:127-127.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (يستفتون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (في النساء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يستفتونك), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "concerning the matter of women"; (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta"; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (يفتي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (في) a preposition and (هنّ) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يفتيكم); (الواو) conjunctive; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, maʿṭūf (conjoined) on the Name of Majesty «[Note: or in the position of the genitive, conjoined on the genitive pronoun in His saying (فيهنّ), i.e. "concerning them and concerning what is recited to you" ... and this is the view of the Kufans, who permit conjoining on a genitive [pronoun] without repeating the preposition.]»; (يتلى) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يتلى); (في الكتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتلى) «[Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (يتلى).]»; (في يتامى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what the preposition phrase (في الكتاب) is attached to, or a badal (substitute) from it with repetition of the preposition, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif; (النساء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (اللاتي) a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of اليتامى; (لا) negating; (تؤتون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as second mafʿūl bihi; (كتب) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (لهن) like فيهن, attached to (كتب); (الواو) conjunctive or circumstantial; (ترغبون) like يستفتون; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (تنكحوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تنكحوهنّ) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, which is implied in two ways: either عن, i.e. "you are averse to marrying them", and then the clause ترغبون is conjoined on the ṣila (relative clause) clause لا تؤتونهنّ ...; or في, i.e. "you desire to marry them", and then the clause ترغبون is circumstantial, i.e. "you do not give them … while you desire to marry them".
(الواو) conjunctive; (المستضعفين) conjoined on (يتامى النساء), genitive like it; (من الولدان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from المستضعفين; (الواو) conjunctive; (أن تقوموا) like أن تنكحوا ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقوموا) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined on (يتامى النساء), i.e. "and concerning your standing for the orphans".
(لليتامى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تقوموا); (بالقسط) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تقوموا); (الواو) resumptive; (ما) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (تفعلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من خير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the omitted pronoun, i.e. "whatever you do of good". (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", i.e. Allah; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (عليما), which is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative.
The clause «يستفتونك ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «الله يفتيكم» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «يفتيكم فيهن» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «يتلى عليكم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the first relative (ما).
The clause «لا تؤتونهن ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (اللاتي).
The clause «كتب لهن» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «تنكحوهن» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the first particle relative (أن).
The clause «تقوموا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «ترغبون» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause لا تؤتونهن.
The clause «تفعلوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كان به عليما» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of (إنّ).

* Morphology:
(يتلى): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion; its origin is يتلو with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the lām; its active past is تلا and its imperfect يتلو, and when it was made passive the letter before the last was given fatḥa, so the wāw was converted to alif because it came vowelled after a fatḥa.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is al-kalām al-muwajjah (double-edged speech), which is speech that bears two opposite meanings; that is in His saying ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾, for they are either beautiful or plain according to how the omitted preposition is implied: في or عن.

* Benefits:
1- A ruling concerning the orphan girl and the young children:
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning this verse: In the Jāhiliyya a man would have an orphan girl in his care whose affairs he had taken charge of, and he would throw his garment over her, and then no one could ever marry her after that. If she was beautiful and he desired her, he married her and consumed her wealth; and if she was plain, he kept men from her forever until she died, and when she died he inherited from her.
So Allah forbade that and prohibited it.
And he said concerning His saying ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدانِ﴾: In the Jāhiliyya they did not give inheritance to the young or to daughters, and that is His saying: ﴿لا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ ما كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ﴾ ... So Allah forbade that and made clear to every holder of a share his share, and said: to the male the like of the portion of two females, young or old.
2- His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: several views have come concerning the i'rab of (ما) in the verse:
1- In the position of the genitive, conjoined on the hāʾ in His saying فيهن.
2- A mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "and We make clear to you what is recited to you".
3- In the position of the nominative, which is the strongest of the views, and in it there are three views: (1) conjoined on the agent pronoun in يفتيكم.
(2) The second: conjoined on the Name of Majesty in His saying: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ﴾.
(3) A mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "and what is recited to you in the Book makes clear to you".
3- His saying, the Exalted, ﴿فِي يَتامَى النِّساءِ﴾: في here has the meaning of the bāʾ, i.e. "because of the orphans", as you say "I came to you on Friday في the matter of Zayd", i.e. "about the matter of Zayd".

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لا) the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā; (تتمنّوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: or a qualified indefinite noun ... and the clause after it is its naʿt (adjective).], (فضل) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فضل), (بعض) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (على بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فضل). (للرجال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (نصيب) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (من) a preposition; (ما) a relative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to a naʿt of (نصيب) [Note: it may be a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar in the position of the genitive.] (اكتسبوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الواو) conjunctive; (للنساء نصيب مما) like (للرجال ... مما); (اكتسبن) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (لنون) [Translator's note: so in the source, for «النون».] an agent pronoun. (الواو) conjunctive; (اسألوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من فضل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اسألوا), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إن الله كان بكل شيء عليما) the i'rab of its counterpart has passed [Note: in verse (29) of this sūra.].
The clause «لا تتمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «فضّل الله ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «للرجال نصيب ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «اكتسبوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the nominal or particle relative (ما).
The clause «للنساء نصيب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (للرجال نصيب).
The clause «اكتسبن» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the nominal or particle relative (ما).
The clause «اسألوا الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (لا تتمنّوا).
The clause «إنّ الله كان ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal.
The clause «كان ... عليما» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.

* Benefits:
1- Disparity among people:
Imām Aḥmad said: Sufyān ibn Abī Najīḥ [Translator's note: so in the source.] narrated to us from Mujāhid, who said: Umm Salama said: O Messenger of Allah, the men go on campaigns and we do not, and we have half the inheritance. So Allah sent down «وَلا تَتَمَنَّوْا ما فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ».

The text is general concerning disparity among people, whether in gifted matters or acquired ones, such as aptitudes, status, goods, and everything in which shares differ in this life.
